Let the years without a champion stand for ever vacant, both as a rebuke and as a tribute. Sometimes, emptiness can be the most eloquent statement of all.

Sports.title: Alexander’s absence weighs heavy as Bradford try to keep promotion push on track
Sports.content:
It was a bruising start to the week for Bradford City when news filtered through to the players that Graham Alexander had stepped down as manager. They were top of League One and his departure was a sudden and unexpected blow for a side that had started to let imaginations run wild about a return to the second tier for the first time in 23 years.

The coaches Mark Trueman and Colin Doyle took interim charge and called a meeting with the squad last Monday. “Some of the players were a little unsettled, didn’t know what was going on or who was taking the team,” Trueman said. “But the players have just got on with business and that’s the key. It shows the mentality of the team. This could quite easily derail them, but they’ve continued to do the right things.”

If any caretaker can keep Bradford on track, it is Trueman, who has now stepped in temporarily five times since joining the club as an Under-18 coach six years ago. This time, though, is different. Previously, his job was to raise the team during low periods. Now the task is to maintain the upward trajectory that began the moment Alexander arrived in 2023.

Bradford were stuck in the bottom tier of the EFL and sitting in 16th when Alexander took over. They finished ninth in his first season, then third in his second to earn automatic promotion, followed by a stunning fourth-place finish back in League One, losing in the playoff semi-finals last May.

It has been a thrilling ride rarely enjoyed by Bradford fans. They twice reached the EFL Trophy semi-finals in successive seasons. At one stage, they won 10 consecutive home games, breaking a club record set in 1953.Last year they had the best home record of any side in Europe’s top five leagues. Alexander won 79 times in 158 games – the best win rate of any Bradford manager in charge for at least 65 games.

The chief executive, Ryan Sparks, said Alexander and the assistant manager Chris Lucketti, who has followed him to Preston, delivered “some of the most incredible moments in our recent history”.

They looked set to deliver more, with Bradford top of League One when the Preston opportunity came out of the blue. Alexander told the club he had ambitions to manage in the Championship, but you wonder if he might have achieved that with Bradford had he stayed. Perhaps he believed that two promotions in two years would risk them becoming relegation fodder in the Championship, whereas Preston presents a more stable platform. Ultimately, the lure of a club that he once captained – playing 400 games during an eight-year spell from 1999 to 2007 – d in the city where his children were raised proved too strong.

View image in fullscreen Graham Alexander’s sudden departure has left Bradford to rebuild early on in the season. Photograph: Paul Thompson/ProSports/Shutterstock

On forums and social media, fans shared a mixture of sadness, anger and anxiety. Most believe Alexander has left the club stronger, but frustration is shared among a sizeable minority about the timing – less than two months into a season after a summer spent recruiting specifically for his aggressive, direct, high-pressing football. After Jake Beesley headed Bradford into a fourth-minute lead at Reading on Saturday, the 1,118 supporters who made the 400-mile round trip sang about being top of the league, but did not chant for their departed manager once.

Rapid developments in the space of a few weeks leave a huge hole. Bradford now find themselves in unfamiliar territory: it is the first time in 43 years they have lost a manager mid-season, and fans are nervous about the executives’ aptitude for finding a suitable replacement, given the shaky record before landing Alexander.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In the opposition dugout at Reading’s Select Car Leasing Stadium stood one of the favourites to take over. Before the match, Leam Richardson faced questions about whether he was interested. His response – that he would be in the Reading dugout for the match – neatly sidestepped the prospect that he might not be beyond this weekend, though he insisted he had not been contacted. Meanwhile Michael Duff, sacked by Wycombe last month, is also being heavily linked.

Nonetheless, Sparks and the head of football, David Sharpe, would have been watching closely from the directors’ box to see whether Reading showed signs of a style of football that would fit the framework Alexander built. Plenty makes Richardson a logical candidate. He previously worked with Sharpe, who was chair at Wigan when Richardson was manager, and he has also coached Callum Connolly, in the Bradford starting XI, and Nick Powell, who came on from the bench.

Others are in the frame, including the Plymouth manager Tom Cleverley, the former Manchester United midfielder – a Premier League winner in 2013 – who at 37 has quietly built his managerial reputation these past two years. Udoka Godwin-Malife’s second-half equaliser meant Plymouth moved above Bradford on goal difference. The next appointment is crucial. Getting Alexander so right makes getting it wrong so much more costly.

Sports.title: Former Chelsea target blocked from switching international allegiance despite nation refusing to play him
Sports.content:
Former Chelsea target blocked from switching international allegiance despite nation refusing to play him

Mile Svilar has once again seen his attempts to switch international allegiance blocked by FIFA.

The Roma goalkeeper has won just one senior cap despite being named Serie A goalkeeper of the year two seasons in a row.



3 Svilar has been prevented from switching back to represent Belgium Credit: Getty

Born in Belgium, Svilar was also eligible for Serbia through his father, a former Yugoslavia international.

After representing the country of his birth at youth level, the 27-year-old made his senior debut for Serbia in September 2021.

Aged 22 at the time, he featured in a friendly against Qatar.

Svilar was subsequently called up once more a month later before changing his mind and opting to switch allegiance back to Belgium.



Svilar blocked from national team switch

However, he has spent the last five years in international football limbo after being blocked from representing the Red Devils.

Meanwhile, Serbia are no longer considering Svilar for selection despite his form for Roma as a result of his change of heart.



FIFA rules allow players to switch national teams even if they have won senior caps.

There are strict rules in place, with such moves only permitted for players who have won less than three caps aged 21 or under.



As Svilar was capped by Serbia as a 22-year-old, he cannot switch back to Belgium despite his only appearance coming in a friendly.

FIFA's rules were expanded in 2020 from friendlies only to all matches outside of major tournaments.

3 Svilar won one cap for Serbia aged 22, preventing him from changing national teams Credit: Getty

Declan Rice was previously allowed to change national teams from the Republic of Ireland to England after featuring in three friendlies for the Boys in Green.



Svilar's stunning Roma form

As for Svilar, he has now been left in the cold on the international stage despite his staggering output in goal for Roma.

Since the start of the 2024/25 season, he has kept a total of 37 Serie A clean sheets.

Across 81 appearances during that period, Svilar has conceded just 69 goals.

His performances have also seen him win the goalkeeper of the year award in each of the last two seasons.



Svilar joined Roma from Benfica back in 2022, having started his career in Belgium with Anderlecht.

3 The former Chelsea target is the two-time Serie A goalkeeper of the year Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, he was rewarded with the new five-year deal last summer.

Chelsea also showed transfer interest in Svilar back in June, according to reports in Italy.

According to Corriere dello Sport, the Blues had a £42.5million bid knocked back by Roma.



Xabi Alonso's side instead went on to sign Emiliano Martinez as their new first-choice goalkeeper.

Sports.title: Summer Man City arrival teases return to old club days after club found guilty of financial breaches
Sports.content:
Summer Man City arrival teases return to old club days after club found guilty of financial breaches

Iliman Ndiaye has hinted he could return to a former club just a month after signing for Manchester City.

The forward penned a five-year deal at the Etihad Stadium after arriving from Everton at the start of September.

3 Ndiaye joined City on a five-year deal in September for an initial £60million Credit: Getty

City completed a £60million deal plus a further £5million in add-ons after hijacking Tottenham Hotspur's move for Ndiaye.

However, he has now teased a surprise return to Marseille three years after leaving the French giants.

It comes just days on from City's guilty verdict in their Financial Fair Play case.

The Premier League announced on Tuesday that the club had been found guilty of all charges against them.

City have since launched an appeal against the ruling.

Meanwhile, Ndiaye has now admitted he has unfinished business at Marseille, where he spent the 2023/24 season.

The Senegal international scored four goals and added five assists in 46 appearances for the club.

Having signed from Sheffield United, he was sold to Everton after just one year in the south of France.

Ndiaye on Marseille return

Speaking to La Provence about his time at Marseille, Ndiaye explained: "The shouts from Marseille supporters asking me to come back? It is nice to hear.

"I don’t think that the story is finished, but we will see. I’m just saying, I never know where it’ll lead me, but we’ll see anyway."

3 Ndiaye has hinted he could one day return to Marseille despite his recent City switch Credit: Getty

Ndiaye helped Marseille reach the semi-finals of the Europa League during his solitary campaign at the Stade Velodrome.

However, a disappointing season domestically saw the club miss out on European qualification by finishing eighth in Ligue 1.

Now at City, Ndiaye has already featured four times in all competitions for Enzo Maresca's side.

Those outings include starts in the Premier League against both Coventry City and Sunderland.

He is still waiting to open his account for the club, though, with zero goals or assists in sky blue to date.

City return to action away at Liverpool on Sunday, October 11 following the international break.

3 Ndiaye has made four appearances since joining City from Everton Credit: Getty

It marks their first match since the guilty verdict was officially announced.

They then host Paris Saint-Germain three days later in the Champions League.

Sports.title: Folarin Balogun makes Premier League transfer admission after Everton move collapsed
Sports.content:
Folarin Balogun has addressed his failed deadline day move to Everton.

The striker had looked set to complete a £40million switch to the Toffees from Monaco at the end of the summer transfer window.

3 Balogun has addressed his Premier League future after his failed Everton move Credit: Getty

However, a significant issue was discovered during his medical, prompting Everton to renogiate the deal.

After agreeing a lower fee with appearance-based add-ons, the move appeared to be back on.

Balogun would then be late for his scheduled flight to England before changing his mind on signing for Everton.

The decision came despite a dealsheet being submitted by the club.

Balogun on future Premier League move

After returning to action with Monaco prior to the international break, Balogun has now addressed the transfer saga.

The USA international spoke exclusively to talkSPORT at the opening NFL London game of the season.

Balogun was in attendance at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium for the Indianapolis Colts' win over the Washington Commanders.

Asked if a Premier League return is still something he would want in the future, the 25-year-old admitted: "Yes, potentially.

"Football has many twists and turns as we’ve seen after the World Cup.

"I was close to a transfer, didn’t materialise, but for sure it’s definitely an option."

3 Balogun saw a deadline day switch to Everton collapse at the 11th hour Credit: AFP

Balogun started his career in England with Arsenal, spending 12 years with the Gunners before his move to Monaco in 2023.

In that time, he made just two Premier League appearances for the club, though.

As for Monaco's campaign so far, he added: "It’s been a good start to the season.

"We’ve started the last three seasons well so I think the focus is how you finish it. So we take it step-by-step."

Filipe Luis' side currently sit top of Ligue 1 with an unbeaten record after five matches this term.

Balogun made his return to action in their win over Lens last time out prior to the international break.

3 Balogun returned to action for Monaco prior to the international break Credit: Getty

It came after he was omitted from their Conference League squad in the wake of his failed move to Everton.

Monaco will face CSKA Sofia, Freiburg, Nordsjaelland, Hearts, Brighton and Lincoln Red Imps during the league phase.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson opens up on health fear as Manchester United legend gives rare interview
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson opens up on health fear as Manchester United legend gives rare interview

Sir Alex Ferguson has expressed his worries over a potential dementia diagnosis during a rare interview.

The Scotsman is known for his legendary spell as Manchester United manager, where he won 13 Premier League titles, five FA Cups, four League Cups and two Champions Leagues.

2 Ferguson, one of the all-time great managers, has admitted his worries over possibly being diagnosed with dementia after his playing career Credit: Getty

Before such a glittering stint on the touchline, Ferguson played as a forward for clubs including Dunfermline Athletic, Rangers and Falkirk.

He also won four caps with Scotland in a career that lasted around 17 years, and is now one of the most famous figures in world football.

During his retirement, Ferguson has worked as an ambassador for Playlist for Life, a Glasgow-based charity that champions personal music playlists for those in dementia care.

The 84-year-old is also an ambassador for Race Against Dementia, an organisation founded by the three-time Formula 1 world champion Sir Jackie Stewart that funds research into the condition.

Ferguson's brother Martin suffers from dementia and now, speaking to The Observer, he is concerned that it could impact him.

What did Sir Alex Ferguson say about his health?

"I worried about that myself because I headed the ball a lot," he said openly when speaking about a charity dinner in aid of Race Against Dementia.

"All footballers did. Dementia’s a challenge for anyone getting older.

"You worry about it a lot. I always say to myself, 'I'm 84 (laughing). If I get to 85, I'll be all right."

On his brother, Ferguson added: "He recognises me, which is great. In Glasgow, they started a music thing (Playlist for Life), and the idea is that you give them a box with all your favourite songs in it.

"They can just press a button to play them, and it brings all the memories back."

2 Ferguson has played a role in the fight against dementia through charity work as research for a cure continues Credit: Getty

Dementia in football

According to Alzheimer's Society, football is a sport that is associated with dementia alongside rugby and American football.

Research has suggested that a reduction in head impact exposure is something that could less then risk of being diagnosed.

Heading is common in football matches, whether it's defenders who are clearing the ball or attackers looking to score.

A 2023 study found that footballers have a 50 per cent increased risk of developing dementia in comparison to the rest of the population.

EFL hero Dean Windass was diagnosed with the condition in 2024, and told talkSPORT he went for a brain scan due to a request from the son of late the England legend Nobby Stiles, John.

Former United star David May has also revealed fears over dementia having estimated that he headed the ball around 20,000 times.

Sports.title: Former Premier League star sacked by non-league club as staff and players left unpaid
Sports.content:
Former Premier League star sacked by non-league club as staff and players left unpaid

Gateshead have sacked manager Lee Cattermole after less than four months in charge.

The National League's bottom club announced the decision on Sunday amid a run of six successive league losses.

3 Cattermole was an icon at Sunderland Credit: Getty - Contributor

Cattermole, who was appointed in June, won just one of his 12 league matches in charge.

Saturday's 2-1 home loss to Worthing leaves the Tynesiders eight points from safety at the foot of the fifth-tier.

It marked the first senior managerial job of Cattermole's coaching career.

He had previously worked with Middlesbrough and Bristol Rovers since retiring in 2020.

Gateshead issue statement on Lee Cattermole

In a post on X, the club said: "The decision follows a series of poor results which have seen the club anchored to the foot of the Enterprise National League table.

"Assistant Manager, Martin Smith, will also leave the club with immediate effect"

Ben Clark has since been placed in caretaker charge by Gateshead.

The first-team coach is set to be in charge against FC Halifax Town next weekend.

Interim chairman Graham Wood added: "The club wishes to thank Lee and Martin for their efforts and wishes them both success in their future careers."

Cattermole's exit comes amid ongoing off-field issues for Gateshead.

3 Cattermole won just one of his 12 league matches in charge of Gateshead Credit: Getty

Gateshead players unpaid

Players and staff have not been paid for September, the club have confirmed.

The managerless outfit have now provided an update after Mark Nellist withdrew his funding.

In a statement shared to X, Gateshead said: "Since Mark Nellist announced his intention to withdraw his funding support from Gateshead Football Club, he has also sought to relinquish his majority ownership of the club.

"He has reached an agreement, subject to approval by the Independent Football Regulator to gift his shares to fellow Gateshead FC shareholder, American-based Stephen Paylor.

"Meanwhile, Paylor has indicated that he is unable to provide funding on his own and was relying on joint-investment from a third part, whose initial strong interest appears to have waned.

In the circumstances, it would appear unlikely that the share transfer from Nellist to Paylor will hain IFR approval. Meanwhile, the club's players and staff remain unpaid.

3 Gateshead have confirmed their players and staff are still unpaid Credit: Getty

"The club is now appealing to the shareholders to continue funding support, thereby giving time to secure fresh investment."

Gateshead are in their fifth season back in the National League following promotion in 2022.

Under Rob Elliott, the club finished 18th last term, eight points above the relegation zone.

Sports.title: Chelsea lead three-way race for new England star Alex Scott as Bournemouth deal runs down
Sports.content:
Chelsea lead three-way race for new England star Alex Scott as Bournemouth deal runs down

Chelsea reportedly lead the chasing pack for Bournemouth star Alex Scott following their unsuccessful summer pursuit.

The 23-year-old is a rising talent in Premier League football and made his England debut on Tuesday in the 2-0 win against Czech Republic.



2 Scott made his first start for England on Saturday and is of interest to three Premier League giants Credit: AFP

Scott then started and played the majority of their 7-0 thumping of Croatia that has put them second in Nations League Group A3.

talkSPORT previously reported that Chelsea had a £64million transfer offer rejected by Bournemouth in the summer.

However, their interest in Scott remains as The Telegraph report that the west Londoners are at the forefront of the queue.



Bournemouth are said to insist that they will not allow a sale during the January transfer window.

Should Scott stay at the Cherries until the end of the season, he will have just one year remaining on his deal.



Arsenal and Liverpool are also credited with interest in the U19 and U21 Euros winner with England.

Chelsea eye more midfield reinforcements

Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson were two midfield arrivals at Stamford Bridge during the summer.



Lamine Camara looked set to be a third from AS Monaco on deadline day, but a move fell through.

Chelsea agreed a £47m deal for the Senegal international, who was set to sign a six-year deal.

Liverpool are understood to have impacted the move by instructing him to stay at Monaco ahead of a potential switch next summer.

2 Chelsea were unable to sign Scott in the summer, but still have him as a midfield target as his deal approaches its last year-and-a-half Credit: Getty



Monaco had also missed out on the sale of Folarin Balogun to Everton on deadline day.

Despite failing to sign Camara, Chelsea still allowed Enzo Fernandez to join Manchester City for £125m.

The Argentina international left the club after three-and-a-half years to reunite with their former head coach Enzo Maresca at City.

Chelsea have been without their key midfield man in Moises Caicedo for most of the season.



Caicedo was brought on as a substitute in their 4-3 win over Brighton but lasted just 14 minutes before going off with injury.

Romeo Lavia has played more frequent minutes following past injury issues, whilst Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli became their youngest-ever player in the Premier League in the 3-0 defeat at Brentford.

Sports.title: England’s next captain debate settled amid Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice battle
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham has been tipped to succeed Harry Kane as England captain by talkSPORT's Henry Winter.

The 23-year-old produced yet another standout display against Croatia on Saturday.



3 Bellingham has been hailed as a 'special player' after another standout display for England Credit: Getty

Bellingham scored and provided three assists for the Three Lions as they claimed a 7-0 away victory in Rijeka.

It takes his tally for England to 14 in 59 caps despite not turning 24 for another eight months.

According to Winter, Bellingham has shown all of the qualities of a future England captain.



The armband is currently held by Kane, who was named skipper back in 2018.

Bellingham tipped for captaincy

Discussing Bellingham's impact on Sunday Edition alongside Shaun Custis, Winter said: "He’s a fantastic role model. He’s a top professional.



"He’s playing for a club which has probably got the most pressure on it in the world and he’s relishing it.

"You saw when he went to Real Madrid, he took (Zinedine) Zidane’s shirt. It was a player he idolised growing up and he was fantastic that season.



"There’s already a debate within the FA and coaching circles about whether he becomes a number nine because we don’t have any centre forwards really coming through at the moment.

"When Harry Kane moves on, whenever it is, the way Kane is playing he is going to be around for a while.

"So he’s a truly special player. He’s England’s next captain for me."

3 Bellingham should be England's next captain in the eyes of Winter Credit: AFP

Bellingham inherited the No.5 shirt upon signing for Real Madrid in 2023.



The midfielder has since made 148 appearances, scoring 49 goals as well as winning four trophies including the Champions League.

However, there appears to be another player ahead of Bellingham in Thomas Tuchel's current captaincy pecking order.

Declan Rice was named vice-captain behind Kane prior to the World Cup in June.

Pearce on Rice

Reacting to the decision at the time, Stuart Pearce told talkSPORT: "I've always viewed Rice from afar… maybe I'm slightly biased towards him as I've worked with him… that he'd thrive in an environment like that.



"I would love to see him as the Arsenal captain, I can't believe that he's not Arsenal captain.

3 Rice was named England vice-captain prior to the World Cup Credit: Getty

"I think he would flourish in the role and he is captain material, so him being England vice-captain is fantastic to see."

Rice is absent from the current squad due to a hamstring injury but is set to return to action following the international break.



The 27-year-old has already won 80 caps for the Three Lions, having made his debut in 2019.

He has also been part of the last four tournament squads along with Bellingham.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel finally solves problem position thanks to six cap England star
Sports.content:
Lewis Hall has more than seized his opportunity to be England's left-back - he deserves a run in Thomas Tuchel's team now.

That is the verdict of Henry Winter on talkSPORT's Sunday Edition, in reaction to the Newcastle defender's impressive form over the break.



3 Hall completed the joint-most dribbles (4) with Jude Bellingham in the 7-0 win over Croatia Credit: AFP

The 22-year-old was a surprise omission from Tuchel's World Cup squad this summer and had to watch the tournament from home.

Lewis Hall revival

Hall paid the price for a downturn in his club form at the back end of last season, which started when he was hooked at half-time of a 2-1 defeat at home to Bournemouth in April.

He was then made an unused substitute for the Magpies' 1-0 loss to Arsenal a week later, and only made a brief cameo in the Premier League match after that - a 3-1 victory over Brighton.



Hall fought his way back into Eddie Howe's XI, but was forced to play out of position at right-back as Dan Burn - who did make the World Cup squad - continued to deputise on the left flank.

The former has now drastically changed his fortunes for both club and country after enjoying a new lease of life under Matthias Jaissle.



Hall earned an England recall after scoring once and registering an assist in five Premier League outings this term.

The ex-Chelsea starlet, who was the subject of considerable transfer interest from Manchester United, is now understood to have signed a new contract at St James' Park.



He has since taken full advantage of Nico O'Reilly's injury to make the England left-back spot his own in the past two matches.

Manchester City's O'Reilly started the first fixture of the break, but endured a howler as he gave away a goal in the 3-2 defeat to Spain.

Hall has since helped England keep successive clean sheets in the victories over Czechia and Croatia, while displaying a strong connection with his former Newcastle teammate Anthony Gordon.

3 Hall and Gordon took their former Newcastle partnership onto the international stage with England Credit: Getty



England's left-back problem

A mixture of fitness and form has meant Hall has been capped just six times for his country and, before this month, had never made an international start under Tuchel.

The Three Lions boss has had significant challenges finding a permanent solution to his first-choice left-back since he took charge.

Shaun Custis told talkSPORT: "One player I think we do agree on about playing left back is Lewis Hall, who of course didn't go to the World Cup.

"I would say I thought Nico O'Reilly had a good World Cup, but Lewis Hall in a kind of orthodox left-back role looked really, really good and has a link-up with Anthony Gordon.



Football journalist Winter added: "Yeah, absolutely. Ever since he was linked with stepping up into the England team, because we've seen the good work that he's sort of done in the England age groups.

3 Hall has now firmly established himself as Tuchel's best left-back option, provided he remains fit Credit: Getty

"England, their starting left-backs: I went through it early this morning," Winter continued.

"[Ben] Chilwell, [Kieran] Trippier, right side, but playing on the left, more so left wing back.



"[Luke] Shaw finally got fit for the Euro final.

"[Levi] Colwill, [Trent] Alexander-Arnold, Lewis, Rico Lewis, now playing left back for the under-21s.

"[Reece] James, [Tino] Livramento, [Myles] Lewis-Skelly, [Djed] Spence and O'Reilly. And I think we should give Lewis Hall a run now."

Sports.title: Erling Haaland limps off during Norway's Nations League clash with Portugal to leave Man City sweating just a week before Liverpool showdown
Sports.content:
Manchester City are sweating over Erling Haaland's fitness after the forward limped off during Norway's Nations League defeat against Portugal on Sunday night.

The 26-year-old had signalled that he wanted to come off with a hand motion during the second half.

His withdrawal comes just a week before Manchester City travel to Liverpool, with their guilty verdict in their batle with the Premier League hanging over them.

The forward was able to walk off the pitch unaided with the score at 1-1, but a 79th-minute goal from Goncalo Ramos saw Portugal win 2-1 in the absence of Cristiano Ronaldo.

Haaland started all four of Norway's Nations League matches in a 10-day spell, scoring in earlier fixture against Denmark and Portugal.

It remains to be seen how much of a headache this could be for City, who also saw Nico O'Reilly withdraw from England duty mid-way through the international break with an injury.

More to follow.

Erling Haaland asked to be subbed and limped off during Norway's 2-1 defeat by Portugal

Haaland has enjoyed a flying start to the season, scoring seven in as many appearances for City, who are top of the Premier League with a perfect record.

He did not get much of a summer break, with Norway having reached the quarter-finals of the World Cup, where they lost to England.

His success is partially built on his capacity to play plenty of games without getting injured. Last season he only missed one match with a knock, and the longest injury of his career in 2023-24 did not even keep him out for two months.

It has been a tough international break for City after the Premier League condemned them for making 'sham' agreements to manipulate their financial accounts to the tune of £900million over a nine-season period which saw them win eight trophies.

On Friday last week, Daily Mail Sport reported how City had been found guilty of 114 of 115 charges against them.

However, there had been no official comment from the Premier League on the findings of an independent panel who oversaw a hearing that concluded in December 2024.

That then dramatically changed. In a lengthy statement, the Premier League say City arranged 'sham contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on "sham" agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs'.

It also says the club falsely altered the financial picture at the Etihad to the tune of £900m. The club had agreed exorbitant sponsorship deals with a number of companies, but those sponsors only paid part of the fee.

The rest was propped up by the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club.

Premier League CEO Richard Masters claimed that the commission's verdict had 'vindicated' the league's decision to pursue the charges

As the Premier League note, this allowed City to 'artificially inflate the club’s revenues' and therefore spend more under Premier League rules. The higher the revenue a club records, the more they are permitted to spend.

Moreover, further 'sham' deals, funded by ADUG, allowed the club to 'record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred'.

The Premier League say that revenues were inflated and costs reduced to the tune of £900m in an attempt to comply with spending rules. The result was that the club 'filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators'.

It added that the club was 'significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits' during the time period in question, 2009-2018 when it won eight major trophies.

Had City reported accurately 'it would have been in breach of both the League's and UEFA's spending limits by a very substantial amount'.

The panel also found that City committed multiple breaches of its duties of co-operation and good faith in that it failed to assist the Premier League's four-year investigation, triggered by the emergence of club emails obtained by a hacker.

Indeed, City had 'made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the PL investigation'.

Richard Masters, Chief Executive of the Premier League, said: 'The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

'It also vindicates the Premier League's decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

'It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

'This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches. Now we have the Commission's decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans.'

Manchester City have insisted on their innocence throughout the saga (Pep Guardiola pictured with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak)

In a statement released a short time later, City said it was ‘disappointed and surprised’ and referred to the ‘opinion of the Premier League Commission’.

It added: ‘The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

‘The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

‘The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete.’

City have until Friday to appeal.

Man City were first charged with the 115 breaches in February 2023. While that totemic number stuck, the figure – as they subsequently corrected – was actually 130.

Of those, 54 were charges of ‘failure to provide accurate and up-to-date financial information’ while there were 14 charges of ‘failure to provide accurate financial reports for player and manager compensation’.

Both sets related to alleged offences between 2009 and 2018 (2009-2018), an eight-year period which saw the club win four Premier League titles, the FA Cup, and three League Cup competitions.

There were also five charges of ‘failure to comply with UEFA’s regulations, including Financial Fair Play Regulations’ and seven charges of breaching the Premier League’s profit and sustainability regulations (PSR) between 2015 and 2018.

There were also 35 counts of failure to co-operate with Premier League investigations between 2018 and 2023.

The hearing into the 130 breaches began last September at London’s International Dispute Resolution Centre, with the Premier League sparing no expense and enlisting KCs Adam Lewis and Andrew Hunter to take its case.

Sports.title: Tom Brady owns up to rookie on-air mistake that sparked technical issues behind the scenes on Fox broadcast
Sports.content:
Tom Brady owned up after accidentally causing audio issues in the Fox Sports booth during their Week 4 assignment.

Brady and the Fox A-team were in Philadelphia to watch the Eagles take on the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field.

But he inadvertently silenced his producers, causing disruption for him and partner Kevin Burkhardt in the first half before realizing what happened and the fact he was to blame in humiliating circumstances later exposed live on air.

'You want to fess up?' Burkhardt asked his partner. 'The mic issue?' before Brady took the opportunity with both hands.

'Okay, my fault,' Brady said. 'I have this big clunky board which I have all this information about what I want to say all day.'

He showed a large fold-up card filled with notes about the two teams, an insight into his level of preparation, before explaining the chaos it caused.

Tom Brady owned up to a humiliating mistake in the Fox booth during NFL Week 4 action

Now that's a QB owning up to his mistake �� @TomBrady https://t.co/wUt5Zagrpz — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) October 4, 2026

'And I dropped it on the talk back button' he continued. 'And I'm sitting here going, 'guys, I can't hear anyone', and it's my fault the whole time.

'That's like a quarterback owning up to his mistakes, that's what it is.'

Brady was back on air for the first time since an explosive, tell-all book about his life was released.

Lars Anderson, the man who wrote 'Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness,' dove into the seven-time Super Bowl champion's split from the actress and his subsequent romance and marriage to supermodel Gisele Bundchen.

The Daily Mail exclusively published the first extract of the book last week sharing the ugly details of his marriage to Gisele and details of their split.

A second extract from the book shared insight into Brady's private life dating back to his college career and the secrets stashed from the years long before his fame.

Anderson, a Sports Illustrated writer, has previously written a book on the Manning Family and explained his desire to try and give readers an insight into who the seven-time Super Bowl champion 'really is' behind the scenes.

'Numerous books have been written about different aspects of Tom Brady's career, but no one has authored the definitive biography on him: a meaty, deeply reported narrative that gives readers a 360-degree view of his iconic life,' Anderson said to PEOPLE.

A new book on Brady's life has shed light on his marriage and divorce with Gisele Bundchen

'This was the goal as I spent two years digging into the bedrocks of Brady to explain him, interpret his story and answer the fundamental question of who he really is.

'I explore what he represents, what makes him tick, and why he inspires so much passion — you either love him or loathe him.

'I looked at why his relationships with the two famous women who bore his children failed, examined the price of genius and probed his category-five obsession with perfection.

'Employing put-you-there storytelling techniques, my goal was to place the reader next to Brady at all the key moments of his life, recreating scenes to show sides never before seen of the winningest player in NFL history.'

PART ONE: Every ugly detail of Tom and Gisele's marriage... the secret letter stashed in a drawer... and her savage last three words

PART TWO: Why Tom Brady's college teammates were convinced he was gay... until one uninhibited night proved the truth: Secrets from his years before fame - and existential crisis that drove him to the brink

Sports.title: Phil Mickelson is tipped for stunning return to the PGA Tour by LIV Golf's biggest critic in the wake of his 'family trauma' rehab
Sports.content:
Phil Mickelson's biggest critic has tipped him for a shock return to the PGA Tour after it emerged he has been in rehab amid ongoing personal issues.

Mickelson reportedly entered and has already left an addiction center. His representatives told TMZ: 'Phil was seeking treatment for family trauma and addiction.'

The news comes after the 56-year-old, a six-time major champion, stepped away from professional golf this year.

In the meantime, LIV Golf has been torn apart after the withdrawal of Saudi funding, leading to questions over the future of its stars.

Brandel Chamblee, now lead analyst on Golf Channel after his own playing career ended, has been the most outspoken critic of those who turned their backs on the PGA Tour for LIV Golf.

He also has a long history with Mickelson in particular, who told GOLF Magazine in 2018: 'He and I don't see eye to eye on anything.'

Phil Mickelson has been tipped for a PGA Tour return after spending time in a rehab facility

Brandel Chamblee has long been one of Mickelson and LIV Golf's most vocal public critics

But Mickelson has found a surprising olive branch from Chamblee, who believes the legendary leftie would be forgiven and welcomed back if he wanted to be.

Speaking on the We Need a Fourth podcast, Chamblee was asked whether Mickelson has tarnished his legacy for good.

'I don't know about forever,' he said. 'I think we're in a pretty forgiving world. He's obviously got his demons that he fights, and I wouldn't wish them on anybody, but he's not alone in fighting demons.

'I think if he hadn't gone to LIV, he would have been Arnold Palmer reincarnated. He would have been Ryder Cup captain numerous times. He would have been an honorary starter at Augusta. He would have been the lead analyst at CBS. He would have been the pied piper everywhere he went.

'But I think if he came back and said 'look, I've made mistakes, I've tried to deal with them. Sorry for the damage I've caused.

'The game's been so good to me. And for the rest of my life, I'm going to try and be good back to it', I think everyone would put their arms around him and go 'welcome back, sorry you had so much trouble, hope you get your life straightened out'.

'Life's hard, it doesn't matter who you're talking into, running into. Everybody's dealing with something. Everybody's got some battle that they've faced or will face.

'I started doing commentary in 2004, so 2004 until Phil left, I used to say Phil was a gift to the game of golf. His talent, his showmanship, his look at me quality, it was incredible. What a talent, what an amazing talent.'

The golfer and his wife are seen taking in the action on the Sunday of the 2021 Ryder Cup

Mickelson and Amy are pictured with their children, Evan, Sophie and Amanda, after his victory at the 2013 Open Championship

Mickelson stepped away from golf earlier this year and cited an unspecified private family matter involving his wife, Amy, for his absence.

Mickelson has been married to Amy, 54, for almost 30 years after tying the knot back in November 1996. The couple share three children together in Evan, Sophie and Amanda.

He has been candid about his struggles with gambling, previously opening up on his addiction in 2023.

He said at the time that he had 'crossed the line from moderation into addiction which isn't fun at all.'

'The money wasn't ever the issue since our financial security has never been threatened, but I was so distracted I wasn't able to be present with the ones I love and caused a lot of harm,' he said.

He also described how this 'lack of presence' has been 'so hurtful' for his family, saying he's been 'often' told throughout his addiction, 'You're here, but you're not with us.'

'It affected those I care about in ways I wasn't aware or could fully understand,' Mickelson said. 'It's like a hurricane is going on outside and I'm isolated in a shelter oblivious to what was happening.'

'When I came out there was so much damage to clean up that I just wanted to back inside and not deal with it,' he added.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon is playing with swagger and belief - and his telepathic connection with Lewis Hall could mean Thomas Tuchel FINALLY solves a problem area in his team
Sports.content:
It’s a goal and an assist once an hour for Anthony Gordon in an England shirt at the moment. Eight of those vital contributions in his last six games since clambering off the bench for the rescue act against DR Congo, another two added to the growing collection during Saturday’s demolition job in Croatia.

Count winning a penalty in the Azteca as the assist it was and the statistics are even more favourable: a goal contribution every 53 minutes.

Whatever the numbers, something has clicked inside somebody who has felt somewhat underappreciated by the English public and actively wanted to leave the Premier League to alter perceptions of his abilities.

Barcelona suits him, the £68million man whose performances in Catalonia are delighting Culers in much the same way as his use of Spanish at the summer unveiling.

Thomas Tuchel has noticed an extra air of confidence to him through this international camp (three goals and an assist), a sense of greater understanding around new-found seniority and a belief that he is now one of England’s main pillars.

Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Bukayo Saka are locks in three of the attacking positions. It’s impossible to argue against Gordon’s inclusion as the fourth after the past few months.

Anthony Gordon (centre) and Lewis Hall (right) have a flourishing understanding

‘Anthony plays with a lot more edge,’ Tuchel said. ‘He’s for sure found another level, another gear, and is very decisive.’ The very best grow the higher they climb.

Gordon believes that Congo, changing the game in Atlanta’s indoor arena when the air was rapidly leaving England’s World Cup balloon, positively shifted his international arc.

By his own admission, it takes him a while to settle within a group – although that hasn’t seemed a problem at Barca – and now approaching 30 caps, it has become time to take ownership of the left wing. Particularly as Marcus Rashford nudged himself back into the frame last season and provided stiff competition in America.

Gordon’s goal in Rijeka on Saturday evening, England’s third of the night, was a flying header to follow up another smart header in Prague days earlier. To highlight just how things are landing for him right now, the former Newcastle United forward has not scored a single header across 248 career club appearances.

There is a swagger, noticeable in how he toyed with markers at the weekend. Josip Stanisic of Bayern Munich will have endured nightmares. The way Gordon stopped an attack dead, stood Stanisic up and then strutted past provided embarrassment for a full back who started both legs of the Champions League semi-final under Vincent Kompany last season. Croatia might as well have picked one of the kids in the stands.

Poor Stanisic was only provided mercy by Slaven Bilic once Gordon had earned his rest, which in itself felt unfair. Yet there might be some relief that the 25-year-old didn’t make the experience even more chastening, missing three big chances across his 70 minutes. It really could, and should, have been 10.

One of those arrived seconds after Kane’s early opener and engineered by Lewis Hall, his former team-mate at St James’ Park. Hall’s had a strong week himself after Nico O’Reilly’s injury and the connection between the two is obvious, a telepathy that Tuchel must want to tap into more.

Quieter and more reserved, Hall is offering evidence that an incisiveness from the middle third – the pass for that Gordon chance had precision and perfect weight – is being matched by defensive doggedness. Possessing both is a rare find in modern full backs.

Gordon's form for Barcelona and England has taken him to a different level this season

To illustrate that, during a brief moment of England panic – Croatia breaking and the visitors defensively misshapen – Hall held up the galloping Franjo Ivanovic to allow others a return to their normal positions and the danger was adequately snuffed. Later on, and with England already five goals up, it was Hall’s relentless pressing inside the Croatia box that prompted a gift for Saka to smash into the net’s roof.

Hall had to deal with the setback of missing out on the World Cup squad and felt he was worthy of a spot, the response being an encouraging start to this campaign and carrying on where he left off for Newcastle. Hall, 23, has spoken openly about having to ‘play catch up’ with Tuchel’s general messaging during the camp, with the majority of the players familiar after seven weeks together Stateside.

Individually things are going well and as a pairing, they look a proper package. Tuchel loves his combinations – Bellingham and Kane, Guehi and Konsa, Quansah and Saka when Reece James isn’t fit. He wants them all over the pitch and the left-hand side has felt like a forever problem for England.

Gordon has unequivocally done more than anybody else to nail down the attacking spot, with Hall now in a straight battle with O’Reilly for the supporting role. Even before this week, the left has appeared in ruder health than for some time.

In the knockout stages of 2021, 2022 and 2024 tournaments, Luke Shaw had the place sorted for himself but there was uncertainty about what lay ahead of him. Phil Foden’s versatility meant he was shunted wide in 2022 and two years later, in a bid to play the Manchester City star inside, Shaw operated as a wing back as Gareth Southgate went to a back three to the detriment of any real flair.

The combinations weren’t quite there and Tuchel has had some questions answered across his tenure, with some crystallised during the first camp of the season.

‘I don’t want to write Nico O’Reilly off because he played for us in the first match,’ Tuchel said. ‘Lewis had two good matches now. He loves to play in the offensive full back position, he’s very good on the ball. He loves ball possession. He is very clinical, loves these little movements.

‘He played very well with Anthony. You can see that they’ve played many seasons together in the coordination of their movements. He helped Anthony a lot.’

Gordon has now taken ownership of the left wing position under Thomas Tuchel

Saturday was their 58th start together for club and country; as Tuchel alluded to, it showed. There is a little more power and physicality than advertised in them, Gordon leaning into his wiry frame and hustling in recovery runs to back up his mate, with Hall’s engine providing a different dimension going the other way.

‘I’m nowhere near the player I can be,’ Gordon told ITV last week when dissecting the move to Barca and his increased international standing. He regularly journals private targets and starring in La Liga appears to have been one. ‘Maybe delusionally I’ve [envisioned] it from a young age. Why would I have so much confidence from a young age? It makes no sense. I can’t explain why.

‘I’ve become a different player in a lot of people’s eyes. I always felt in England that people respected me because I was fast and I pressed but they never actually respected the quality and IQ that I play with. Only the players I play with seem to notice that. Now that I’m at Barcelona and playing a different style, those qualities are highlighted much more and people are starting to take notice that I’m not just quick.’

He spoke at length with Kane about the prospect of Barca, the side effects of leaving familiarities, and given the captain’s explosion at Bayern – in the running for this year’s Ballon d’Or – the feedback was to go for it wholeheartedly.

Gordon has never been shy, Everton fans will tell you that with the way he moved to Newcastle, and is still surprised at coming off against Argentina as England retreated. In being honest with himself in the quest for constant improvement and proving he deserves a place on this stage, he vows to become more selfish around the box.

Five assists in his first four Barca matches suggests that might need a bit of work. Not a lot else does and it is inarguable that Gordon looks even slicker with his mate behind him.

Sports.title: Former Premier League boss Jesse Marsch claims 'EVERYONE knew' about Man City's cheating - and calls for club to be relegated after guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Former Premier League boss Jesse Marsch claims 'EVERYONE knew' about Man City's cheating - and calls for club to be relegated after guilty verdict

Former Leeds United manager Jesse Marsch has insisted 'everyone knew' about Manchester City's cheating and has called for the club to be relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching financial rules.

Marsch was appointed as Leeds boss in February 2022 but was sacked 12 months later as the club battled to avoid relegation from the Premier League.

The 52-year-old, who is now in charge of Canada, was asked about an independent commission ruling verdict that ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period peppered with ‘sham’ deals.

In a damning 40-page verdict, published on Tuesday, found City artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

While the ruling covered the period between 2009-2018, Marsch expressed his belief that there were 'inconsistencies' even during his time in the Premier League.

Marsch told the Guardian that Man City should be relegated from the top flight as a result of the verdict. Man City confirmed on Friday that they have lodged an appeal to overturn the independent commission's verdict.

Jesse Marsch, left, has claimed 'everyone knew' about Man City's cheating as he called for the club to be relegated from the top flight

Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of charges against them by the Premier League, but have launched an appeal against the decision

'I think Man City should be punished severely. I think they should have to go down, and by the way, everyone knew about it. Everyone knew,' Marsch said.

'That summer [2022], us and Man City were the only teams that said we made money.

'For us, we did make money, because we sold Raphinha, we sold Kalvin Phillips [to City]. We had a lot left over from what we bought.

'At the time, we weren't in a position financially to not save. Our ownership didn't have deep pockets.

'Whereas when Man City says this, I was literally like, "Are you kidding me? Is this some kind of joke?"

'When they said they got Erling Haaland for £52m, it's like: "Yeah, OK, sure".

'So, I knew there were inconsistencies in it, but what can you do? You just put your arms in the air and go, "This is football".

The 2022 summer referred to by Marsch had seen clubs reveal their accounts for the 2020-21 season, which had been played behind closed doors due to the Covid-19 pandemic.

Marsch questioned Man City announcing profits in the summer of 2022, along with questioning their £52m deal to sign his former player Erling Haaland from Borussia Dortmund

Man City signed Kalvin Phillips from Leeds in the summer of 2022 in a £42million transfer

Leeds announced an operating profit of £5.5m, with the club's income having been boosted by their return to the top flight following promotion from the Championship the previous campaign.

Man City reported a narrow £2.4m profit in the same period having reported losses of £126m in the 2019-20 season.

The club's run to the 2021 Champions League final and their fourth Premier League title under Pep Guardiola were cited as key reasons for their financial success.

Marsch's comments also highlighted the summer transfer window in 2022, which saw Man City sign Haaland for £52m and bring in Phillips from his Leeds side in a £42m deal.

Leeds also sold Brazilian star Raphinha to Barcelona for £55m, with the club using the finances from both deals to fund close to £140m of incomings.

Leeds, who sacked Marsch in February 2023, were relegated at the end of the season.

Daily Mail Sport reported last week that the Premier League could review transactions following 2018, the final year covered by their investigation into Man City.

Man City's appeal against the independent commission verdict was made on Friday, with the club stating it 'maintains its innocence'.

Much of their defence will claim commercial contracts were paid for by the Abu Dhabi government rather than their owner.

Sports.title: England's Euros rivals will be running scared after seven-goal Croatia demolition, claims new star Alex Scott - as Rico Lewis earns first call-up in two years
Sports.content:
New England midfield star Alex Scott believes the rest of Europe will have been scared by Saturday’s 7-0 demolition of Croatia in Rikeja.

The Bournemouth player made his first England start alongside his friend Elliot Anderson as Thomas Tuchel’s team tore the Croats apart in the Nations League.

Croatian legend Luka Modric has admitted he was left ‘ashamed’ by the outcome and Scott believes this may just be the start for Tuchel’s team.

‘It's important to put these markers down and beat teams like that to scare opposition in the future,' said Scott.

‘It was my first start and they don't come much better than that. Seven goals and we were deadly from the off.

‘The front four were unbelievable and it makes it easy playing behind that. Anthony Gordon is deadly making runs in behind, with his pace and ability, and Jude Bellingham was everywhere on the pitch.

Alex Scott says England's European rivals will be scared by their potency against Croatia

The England new boy described Jude Bellingham as 'the best midfielder in the world'

‘Honestly, I've never seen anything like it.

‘He's even better in person, seeing it up close and being on the same pitch as him. He's the best midfielder in the world, one of the best players in the world for sure and a great human being.

‘On the pitch his ability is scary and that's the benchmark we need to live up to. I'm the same age as him but for me he's a role model figure for young English players.’

One youngster who may get a chance to prove himself against the Czech Republic on Tuesday is Rico Lewis, who has been added to the senior England squad for the final game of the international break. The Manchester City star last played for the Three Lions first team in 2024.

Saturday’s defeat was the heaviest in Croatian history. Modric started the game even though he celebrated his 41st birthday last month.

Afterwards the former Spurs and Real Madrid star said: 'It is difficult to find an explanation for a performance like that, with no duels, fouls, aggression or cohesion.

‘I have been here for 20 years, but it is the first time I have felt ashamed after a match.

'You can lose, someone can be stronger, at the moment they are stronger, but losing in this way and throwing away the reputation we have built up over all these years is unacceptable.

‘I really do feel ashamed.'

Luka Modric said he was 'ashamed' after the match after the heaviest loss in Croatian history

Rico Lewis has been added to the England squad for the final match of the international break against Czechia on Tuesday

Meanwhile England boss Tuchel will lead his team into the final of four Nations League games at home to Czech Republic on Tuesday acknowledging that several of his squad have made steps forward in the absence of senior names such as Decal Rice and Cole Palmer.

Asked about whether Scott, 23, could challenge Rice for a central midfield berth in the long term, Tuchel said: ‘Of course, and he does.

‘We need performances like this.

‘This is just the nature of it, and we will not survive on two central midfielders. The more the better. And it's always about the guys who are in camp.

‘Declan knows about his importance, and he's one of the very best midfielders in Europe. Nothing will change that.

‘But it's exactly what we need. We need more, more, more, more variety. We need more, more, more options.

‘And it's always then, in the end, about the guys who are in camp. And Alex has been at the highest level.’

Sports.title: Daryz claims back-to-back Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe to establish his place among flat racing's greats
Sports.content:
Daryz produced a devastating display in the Paris sunshine to capture a second Qatar Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe and establish his place among flat racing’s greats.

Only three colts have returned to defend their crown in the Arc since the end of the second world war, with none managing the feat since Alleged in 1978.

However, Francis-Henri Graffard’s exceptional four-year-old eagerly grasped his moment in time on the Bois de Boulogne, delivering his trademark turn of foot in the Longchamp straight under Mickael Barzalona to run down the gallant Bay City Roller and score by a length-and-a-quarter.

The victory took the winner’s course record to a remarkable eight victories from nine starts at the Paris venue, but hopes of seeing him trying to complete a record-breaking hat-trick next autumn were swiftly expunged with a stud career now awaiting the brilliant son of Sea The Stars.

‘I was never worried,’ said owner Princess Zahra Aga Khan, who took over the racing operation of the Aga Khan Studs following the death of her father last year.

‘He has such a will to win, and such speed, I was pretty relaxed.

Daryz has won back-to-back Qatar Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, cementing his place among the flat racing greats

‘Last year was especially tough as I was caught up in the moment and still dealing with the loss.’

Referring to her colt’s future, she added: ‘You get to the point where you're taking a risk every time you run the horse.

‘His mother improved with age but would we want him to train on for another year? I’m not sure. He has other things to do.’

Whereas Daryz’s owner was fairly relaxed throughout, the brilliant Graffard admitted to plenty of pre-race nerves.

‘I really felt the pressure for the last fortnight,’ he said.

‘I tried to remain zen but it is difficult to do so and the weight on my shoulders was enormous when he went into the stalls before the race.

‘But he is such a great champion that once he got a clear run I was more relaxed.’

‘I am a trainer and I like to race, so I wish to try for a third time, but I don't think I will be allowed. I think that would be too much pressure!

‘I don't think he has to prove anything else, it has been beautiful to watch and it was beautiful to watch a champion like him win a race like that.’

For George Scott, trainer of Bay City Roller, defeat brought mixed emotions: ‘I could see Daryz coming. We came up second-best to an outstanding racehorse. Congratulations to the connections.

‘I’m proud of our horse. He’ll go to the Champion Stakes now and hopefully we’ll get a little bit of rain.’

Fellow UK raiders Friendly Soul, Kalpana and Maltese Cross were fourth, fifth and sixth respectively, but there was British Group 1 success on the card for Karl Burke and rider Jack Nicholls with Miss Yechance in the Prix de l’Abbaye, while John & Thady Gosden claimed the Prix de l’Opera courtesy of the Christophe Soumillon-ridden Miss Scott.

Sports.title: Formula One drivers lash out at farcical Bahrain Grand Prix after 'software' issue caused chaos in Malaysia - as Lewis Hamilton compares bizarre scenes to 'LEGO race'
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton likened Sunday's farcical 'Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia' to a 'Lego race' - a PR stunt he hated at Silverstone in July.

Meanwhile, the governing FIA launched an urgent investigation into the shambles of an event delayed for more than an hour.

This comes after several cars broke down in Kuala Lumpur with software problems on one of Formula One's strangest of days.

Max Verstappen won convincingly but the event will be remembered for the fact that cars could not race in the wet. The software in the half-electric/half-combustion engine power units was exposed to rain for the first significant time and could not cope in such conditions. There was a delay in proceedings lasting 1hr 33min as the technology was rebooted and the race finally went on.

Kimi Antonelli finished second and Hamilton, who drove well after falling back to 18th, finished third, on an afternoon that represented a slap in the face to those who conceived this year's preposterous regulations.

The grand prix, relocated from the Middle East, was pushed back 40 minutes as the rain fell and was delayed for nearly a further hour as gremlins struck on the initial formation lap.

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton were in agreement after the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia

A software issue meant the cars were unable to handle the wet track in Malaysia

Both Verstappen and Hamilton, who denounced the pre-race tour in Lego-built buggies in July ahead of the British race, to a near or total standstill.

'I am pressing the throttle, and nothing is happening,' complained Hamilton, who stopped at the side of the track.

The grand prix was then postponed while the software was rebooted – the most visible sign of the complexity of this year's hybrid engines with their baffling battery components, understood by practically nobody.

Hamilton said: 'It was like the Lego race.'

He added: 'I hope there is a lesson learned.'

The FIA issued a statement within an hour, saying: 'On the formation lap an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit's sector configuration led to an unintended loss of power for a number of cars.

'The FIA Technical Department removed the energy limit constraint in the affected sectors through an updated software release distributed to all competitors during the race delay caused by heavy rain, enabling teams to make the necessary changes to the power unit before the start of the race.'This issue had not been detected by the FIA or the teams during testing or the laps to the grid. The FIA, together with the teams and power unit manufacturers, will undertake a full review of the issue.'

George Russell, who retired with engine failure while lying third, fell 84 points behind championship-leader Antonelli. There are 183 points to be fought over the concluding seven rounds.

Russell said: 'The whole day felt like a bit of a faff, with the delay, the red flag, and endless laps behind the safety car.

'It didn't feel very F1 today. I would be disappointed if I was in the stands and watching that unfold.'

Verstappen, claiming his first win of the season, has been a consistent critic of this year's regulations.

He said: 'What can you say? That's not what you want for the sport.'
