Sports.title: FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay
Sports.content:
The FIA has given insight into why Formula 1 cars experienced technical issues ahead of Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The start of the Sepang race was delayed by 40 minutes due to a downpour; then a chaotic formation lap saw the likes front-row starters Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton suffer from a glitch which rendered throttle input ineffective, with numerous cars coming to a standstill. The red flag was waved.

The situation was branded “unacceptable” by Sergio Perez, who likened it to ‘being in a rental kart and running out of time’; Lando Norris described it “just horrible” and evidence that “we shouldn't have any of that stuff, the electronic side”, given this was linked to Formula 1’s new machinery, which features 47% electrical power.

FIA single-seater Nikolas Tombazis has now explained that, given F1 had never had competitive running in actual wet conditions this season, it was caught out by the power unit’s reaction to cars driving extremely slowly at that time. A software update therefore had to be carried out, hence a 53-minute delay to get the race restarted.

“We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked, because there's been very little wet running this year, and there was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in,” Tombazis said.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“Basically, the formation lap, some cars went very slowly, almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars, and some cars almost stopped completely. And that bug prevented the power to be redeployed and for the cars to start again. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time and not to have such a situation.”

Tombazis praised the FIA’s reaction when it came to fixing the issue as swiftly as possible.

“Once the problem happened, our guys realised very quickly what was happening and had to work under a lot of time pressure for an update to the software, which was issued to the teams, and the teams had to install it on their cars,” he added.

“So all of that took about 20 minutes. It may have felt like five hours for spectators waiting [for] a race and for everybody else, which is understandable, and we are sorry about that. But I think it was quite a fast reaction given the problem.”

Not everyone was so upset about some cars running into trouble, with eighth-placed Fernando Alonso joking at the end of an unusually good day for Aston Martin-Honda: “I had 50% DNFs this year, they never stopped the race for us.”

Sports.title: Russell: “You’ve got to laugh” at bad luck as F1 title drifts away
Sports.content:
Mercedes driver George Russell labelled his misfortune as laughable following Formula 1’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, where a power unit failure cost him a podium finish late on.

Russell was a lowly seventh on the grid at Sepang, but the correct choice of intermediate tyres on a damp track and a lightning getaway saw him surge to second into Turn 1, behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Russell was however passed by Max Verstappen as early as lap six, but the first safety car period gave him a chance to sweep past Antonelli around the outside of Turn 5 at the restart as the race leader dropped down to third – though the Italian youngster found a way back into second place just eight laps later.

Further drama did not disrupt the status quo in the top three, but a late safety car meant Russell had a chance to challenge his rivals for victory. However, the chance never came as a power unit failure took him out of the race before the final restart.

“You've almost got to laugh,” Russell told Sky Sports F1 after his third retirement this season – his second purely technical DNF. “It's beyond disappointment. It's just, so many times this season it's happened.

“Of course, it's a real shame, but… Just keep on fighting. Just keep on trying to go.

“The podium, of course, looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

“Not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling and these questions, let's say.”

As he said, Russell will “keep on fighting”, but is equally aware of his deficit to championship rival Antonelli reaching an unprecedented 84 points.

The Briton steered clear of any sensational comments – he won’t say the title is out of reach – but his assessment is bleak nonetheless.

“I don't need to say I think it's gone or whatever,” he added. “But, of course, it’s exceptionally unlikely, and that's just the reality.

“I knew if I wanted to come back I needed luck on my side. Unfortunately, I've had luck not on my side. So, you know, a three-point loss today being behind Kimi turned into an 18-point loss. Of course, if the issue was on the other side, it would have been an 18-point gain.

“So, yeah, it's a real shame. It's a real shame, but that's just how it is.”

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said the Bahrain GP in Malaysia had been one of his “worst experiences” personally, as Red Bull claimed its first victory of the year over the Silver Arrows and Russell suffered that setback.

“I'm so massively annoyed,” Wolff told Sky. “I'm not in a happy place.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

“We didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will. Then the race literally went, if you consider the fight with Lewis [Hamilton] behind, went against us. We had such an advantage, one VSC, two safety cars. I mean, you couldn't be more unlucky. And to make things worse, PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points.”

After praising Antonelli for ‘doing the job’, the Austrian added: “It's just this overarching topic, the DNFs, that could cost us dearly also for the remaining seven races. A championship is quickly turned around against you or for you if you have a DNF, and that's why that can't continue.”

Perhaps Wolff was overdramatic there. At Sepang, Mercedes was outscored by Ferrari for just the first time since the summer break, and the Scuderia still is 151 points in arrears in the constructors’ championship. Meanwhile, Hamilton’s deficit to Antonelli in the drivers’ standings is up to 106 points.

Asked how to pull the team together after such a result, Wolff replied: “I think we have a good action plan. James [Allison, technical director] is really fully on top of it with his leadership team.

“That lifts my mood because I know we have such a tremendous group of people. In the same way as we have with HPP, they're going to sort it out. But that gives me real relief for the moment to know they are the best and they are going to find a solution. And I think we will come back strong.”

Sports.title: F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Verstappen wins chaotic race from Antonelli as Russell retires late on
Sports.content:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won a disorderly Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, clinching his first victory of the season, as George Russell’s title hopes dwindled further with a late retirement.

After the race was delayed by an hour and a half due to dysfunctional software on a wet track, Verstappen outduelled both Mercedes to triumph as Russell was struck by a technical issue.

After a 40-minute delay due to a downpour, the formation lap began, with Isack Hadjar having a trip through the gravel as the whole field warmed up intermediate tyres. Several cars, including front-row starters Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, suffered software glitches that rendered throttle input ineffective. The red flag was waved, which delayed the race by a further 53 minutes.

When race finally got under way, only nine cars opted for intermediate tyres, including Verstappen, Kimi Antonelli, Russell and Hadjar. Others like Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri went for slicks, like Pierre Gasly, who spun out behind the safety car on lap one and dropped to 13th.

A standing start took place at the end of lap two, as Piastri, Gabriel Bortoleto, Lance Stroll, Nico Hulkenberg made late pitstops to switch from slicks to intermediates.

The Silver Arrows of Antonelli and Russell surged to the front of the pack easily at lights out, despite polesitter Verstappen having the same intermediates; the four-time world champion only narrowly held off Liam Lawson for third, with the Racing Bulls man enjoying a blistering getaway too.

Meanwhile, the Ferraris dropped down the order, along with Norris. Having clipped Nico Hulkenberg’s Audi, Leclerc pitted at the end of that lap and moved to intermediates, while team-mate Hamilton and his compatriot lost further dozens of seconds trying to make their gamble work – along with the Alpines, Oliver Bearman, Fernando Alonso and Valtteri Bottas.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

Verstappen passed Russell for second place in Turn 4 on lap six, with the top three drivers within three seconds while fourth-placed Lawson was 10 seconds down; he was overtaken by Hadjar at the last corner on that same lap.

Verstappen caught Antonelli and started putting pressure on the race leader on lap eight; Antonelli went wide at the last corner but retained the lead.

Bottas-induced safety car levels the field

Bottas lost control in Turn 13 on lap nine and ended up benched in the gravel, causing a safety car period that was perfect timing for the inter-shod runners to switch to slicks, as the latter had become the quicker tyre compound, while allowing those who gambled on slicks to cut their losses.

Antonelli led from Verstappen, Russell, Hadjar, Lawson, Ocon, Lindblad, Sainz, Bortoleto and Piastri, with a variety of slick tyre compounds out on track – most interestingly the Mercedes drivers on mediums and the Red Bulls on softs – while Hamilton, Norris and Leclerc were down in 15th to 17th, with the Ferraris on softs and Norris on hards.

A ruthless Verstappen went around the outside of Antonelli at the restart in Turn 1, while Russell swept past in Turn 5, with the championship leader dropping to third in a few seconds. Meanwhile, Bortoleto and Sainz collided, with the Williams collapsing to 18th and the Audi driver handed a 10-second penalty.

As Verstappen pulled away from the Silver Arrows by over three seconds, Antonelli was getting impatient behind his team-mate, but team orders were not on the cards, so the Italian youngster found a way past in Turn 4 on lap 21. Further down the field, Hamilton was overtaking his opponents one after another, climbing to fifth by lap 22, while Leclerc broke into the top 10 on the following tour.

Antonelli went wide at the last corner and hit the pit entry bollard on lap 24, losing another two seconds to Verstappen, with the gap up to 7.5 seconds. He was now just one second ahead of Russell, but both gaps subsequently increased.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

The wave of second pitstops began on lap 29 for frontrunners, including Russell on lap 32, moving to softs – too early to his taste. Antonelli logically followed on the next tour to avoid being undercut, and so did Verstappen, now comfortably leading by 11 seconds.

Verstappen (briefly) cedes lead under VSC, Russell retires

As Hadjar found himself under pressure from Hamilton, the virtual safety car neutralised the race, with Alex Albon stopped due to a technical failure. Verstappen opted for a ‘cheap’ pitstop but ceded the lead to Antonelli; both Ferraris also changed tyres.

Mercedes eventually opted to pit both cars on the following tour, along with most frontrunners, until the VSC turned into a full safety car – which swayed the remaining ones.

Ahead of the final laps in green-flag conditions, Verstappen led Antonelli, Russell, Hadjar, Hamilton, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Lawson and Alonso, who fought his way into the top 10.

But before racing even got back under way, Russell stopped trackside with a technical issue and retired, while Norris was surprised by cars slowing down ahead and had a trip through the gravel and fell to 11th.

There were just four laps remaining when the safety car returned to the pitlane, and Verstappen mastered the restart; he never was at threat from Antonelli and triumphed. Hamilton found a way past Hadjar in Turn 1 on lap 53, clinching his first podium finish since Silverstone. The Frenchman also dropped behind the sister Ferrari of Leclerc.

Piastri finished sixth ahead of Lawson, while a combative Alonso held off Norris for eighth. Lindblad scored the last available point in 10th, underlining another strong day for Racing Bulls relative to the rival Alpine squad.

Having held sixth place early on, Esteban Ocon collapsed to 15th under the chequered flag, behind team-mate Bearman.

Sports.title: F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia descends into chaos as car trouble prompts red flag
Sports.content:
The Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia has been red-flagged after several cars suffered power unit gremlins during a wet set of formation laps.

After a heavy tropical thunderstorm, the action at Malaysian Sepang was set to get underway with a number of laps behind the safety car followed by a standing start.

But ahead of F1's first-ever wet event under the 2026 regulations, a number of cars suffered power unit gremlins in the rain, suspected to be software related.

Initially, polesitter Max Verstappen reported a lack of acceleration from his Red Bull before the Dutchman got going again. Soon after, second-placed Lewis Hamilton reported a similar issue on his Ferrari, with the Briton crawling around the first formation lap as the rest of the field passed him. One lap later, Hamilton too managed to get going again.

More cars, including Racing Bulls man Liam Lawson, Audi driver Gabriel Bortoleto and Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas, also appeared to struggle with similar problems, with race control suspending the start procedure and throwing a red flag.

With the grid mixed up as cars streamed into pitlane, race control will revert to the original grid positions when the running is resumed.

Race control eventually announced a start time of 16:33 local time, amounting to what would be a 50-minute delay.

Sports.title: F1 Bahrain GP in Malaysia start delayed as thunderstorms hit Sepang
Sports.content:
The start of Formula 1's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia has been delayed due to heaving thunderstorms hitting the Sepang circuit.

As teams formed on the starting grid for the pre-race procedure, a small drizzle turned into a full-blown tropical thunderstorm and a downpour and lightning hit the circuit outside Kuala Lumpur. The sudden torrential rain was so severe that FIA race control had no choice to delay the race start, awaiting improving conditions.

Going out on a reconnaissance lap, the FIA's medical car reported a significant amount of standing water around the track, making the conditions unsuitable to racing.

The FIA's official weather provided expected the rest of the afternoon to be relatively dry once the current system clears Sepang: "Prolonged dry conditions are expected after this shower clears."

The race, exceptionally held in Malaysia due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, is F1's first wet weather event since the 2025 Belgian Grand Prix, and therefore a wet race debut for the all-new 2026 generation of cars.

FIA Medical Car kicks up spray in the pit lane.

As part of the 2026 regulations, drivers will not be allowed to use the boost mode to provide an additional power spike as an overtaking aid. Active aerodynamics can only be partially activated, with only the front wing flap moving and the rear wing staying shut.

Maximum electric deployment will also be reduced, limiting torque and improving car control in low-grip conditions.

After standing in water in a couple of corners was deemed to have cleared sufficiently, race control gave the 10-minute start signal for a formation lap at 15:40 local time.

The race is expected to start with at least two laps behind the safety car to monitor conditions, before intending to execute a standing start procedure.

Sports.title: Why Malaysia would be the perfect place for F1’s first wet-weather race in 2026
Sports.content:
While Formula 1 has already reached the 16th round of the 2026 season, fans have still not been treated to a wet-weather race under the new regulations – or even a wet session. Rain has threatened on several occasions, but the on-track action has consistently remained unaffected.

Following initial concerns about safety in wet conditions, the FIA has made several changes to this year’s regulations. These include increasing the tyre blanket temperatures for intermediates, capping electrical power and, related to that, banning boost mode in the wet.

Aside from that, there are also concerns about the tyres. Several drivers have said that they struggled to get the intermediates up to temperature – and subsequently keep them there. It meant Pirelli was quite keen to have a wet-weather race in Miami, where ambient temperatures are high, while a potential wet race in Montreal was described as “the perfect storm” due to the low temperatures and a layout where it is difficult to get the tyres up to temperature anyway.

In Canada, McLaren did start on intermediates, although that turned out to be the wrong choice as further rain failed to materialise. And so F1 is still waiting for its first wet-weather race under the new technical regulations.

While drivers still have some concerns about safety even after the FIA’s changes – Isack Hadjar called it “dangerous” – Pierre Gasly sums up the feeling of many in the paddock: the Sepang International Circuit would effectively be the ‘easiest’ location for a wet-weather race in 2026.

“I think out of any track in the season, if one is good for wet, it's probably here,” Gasly said when asked about a potential wet-weather race by Autosport.

“If you'll ask me about Vegas in crazy cold conditions and, well, it still could happen there, but then it is definitely going to be more tricky.

Pierre Gasly, Alpine Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

“But here the track is really rough, it's really hot and there's a bit of elevation change as well, so it should be pretty good to clear the track in terms of water quantity. So I think it will be fine.”

Gasly’s experiences with the 2026 car in the wet so far have not been positive, but those conditions were not representative of what drivers could potentially face in Malaysia: “The only time I tried was in January at Silverstone, which was horrendous. And then in Magny-Cours with extremely cold conditions, which didn't feel good at all. But I expect it to be in a much better place here.”

It is a theory shared by tyre supplier Pirelli. Chief engineer Simone Berra acknowledges that Sepang is also the best possible location for them to test the wet-weather tyres.

“I would like to gather some information because it's good to have feedback, not just from our tests, but also from normal running with all the teams and all the drivers,” Berra confirmed when asked about the prospect of rain by Autosport.

“Honestly, as an engineer, I would like to have some more feedback and data to work with. And, yes, this is the perfect circuit to have rain.

“When we went to Montreal, I said it would be the perfect storm because it was cold with a low-energy circuit, but here it's a completely different story.”

Rain is seen on the pitwall Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

It means that if there are problems with the tyres, they will be of a very different nature from those feared in Montreal. There, drivers could have struggled to get the tyres up to temperature, while in Malaysia the opposite could be the case – not only because of the high temperatures, but also due to the extremely rough asphalt.

“The point is that we could end up in a situation where you generate overheating, especially if it's raining and then dries up quite quickly”, Berra said. “So the overheating effect could be important.”

Another atypical factor is that teams generally want to use the full wets as little as possible, but Pirelli expects a different situation in that respect as well at the circuit near Kuala Lumpur.

“When it rains here, it's quite massive and I would see the full wet as the preferred race tyre,” Berra said. “That is probably for once, because we know that usually teams prefer the intermediates. But we also know that here it's often like a monsoon and you need to have proper water dissipation for that.

“But let's first see if it's going to rain or not, because this is probably the first year that we are at round 16 without rain! But if it comes, then I think the full wet is not to be discarded, despite that tyre overheating very quickly. With a high level of standing water, I think it would work quite well.”

Sports.title: Hamilton suspects he could have fought for win had he not started on slicks | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes he could have fought for victory at Sepang had he started on the right tyres.

The Ferrari driver qualified on the front row of the grid alongside Max Verstappen

“We were having a good weekend,” he said. “The car felt great in qualifying. It felt amazing to get to second.

“Me and my engineers were here ’til 11:30 last night just going over everything and I really, really felt today was the opportunity to have at least a good battle with Max.”

The original start was delayed due to rain. A further delay followed after a software problem caused several drivers, including Hamilton and Verstappen, to slow to a crawl during the formation lap.

“My power didn’t come back and I had to stop on-track and restart the car and then we all ended up in the pit lane,” said Hamilton. “Thankfully, we all got back to our positions.”

By the time race control were ready to start the race, the track had dried considerably, though it was still damp. Hamilton and his team chose to start the race on slick tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“There was such a long wait and we were debating what tyre to go on to. And I said, ‘look, there was a lot of spray on the laps to the grid.’

“I went into the pit lane, I looked at the ground, I was like, ‘It’s still wet.’ I went to the pit wall and I was like, ‘It’s still wet.’ And they’re like, ‘Yeah, but because it’s been so long, it’s definitely going to dry up real quick and maybe we’re already in the crossover.’

“So, anyway, as a team we ended up taking that soft and when we were at the end of the pit lane and these two took off their blankets and they were on inters [I knew] we were in trouble.”

The track took a long time to dry and those who opted for intermediates gained a significant advantage at the start. Hamilton urged the team not to bring him into the pits for another change.

“As everyone had overtaken me, they’re like, ‘we stop.’ [But] I know we’ve already [lost] another 26 seconds, what’s the difference from that with one minute 40 or whatever I was down? So I [said] ‘let’s just wait it out for the track to dry.’ And once it did, it felt good that I was catching people.”

Hamilton began to make progress on his softs once the Safety Car came out and he was back within range of other cars.

“The car felt great then after that. Really good pit stops from my guys in the garage and then good strategy.

“For us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case. But, of course, I’m really, really grateful that we managed to get back here.”

He said he will have an “open dialogue” with the team about the decision to start the race on slicks.

“We’ve definitely got areas that we need to improve and we know that, and we’re not in any denial of that.

“So I think we’ll have a constructive chat, we’ll regroup, we’ll take the positives from this weekend, which was the car was really good, and we’ll come back next week fighting. Sports.title: Formula 1 must learn lessons from formation lap shambles at Sepang – Hamilton | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen were unimpressed with the delay to the start of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The pair urged Formula 1 to learn lessons from the software problem which struck both their cars during the original formation lap. Both drivers and several of their rivals slowed to a crawl, leading F1 to abandon the attempt to start the race.

“It was insane,” said Verstappen. “At some point we were five-wide on the straight because we couldn’t understand what was going on.

“Then we did a lap and then I see eight other cars crawling still, and I saw [Hamilton] crawling.”

“That’s not what you want, right, for the sport,” he added.

Hamilton’s Ferrari came to a complete stop. “I had to stop on track and stop the car and engine and restart it,” he said. “I’ve never done that before.”

“I hope there is a lesson learned,” he added.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Race control summoned the field into the pits and distributed revised software parameters to all the teams in order to address the problem. The problem added almost an hour to the original delay, caused by rain.

“They had to update the software and then you have to load it into the car,” said Hamilton. “I guess some had some faster laptops than others.”

The FIA confirmed it “removed the energy limit constraint in the affected sectors through an updated software release” to address the problem.

“It was just like driving at 35 kilometres, going uphill, actually losing speed,” Verstappen explained. “I don’t know exactly, because when you go too low in speed and too low RPM, for whatever reason, then it just bogs down, and normally it takes one or two seconds and it comes back.

“That’s basically also what I had in the start. But somehow that didn’t trigger in the first software round, and then in the second software round it was a bit better, luckily.”

Sports.title: FIA blames “unprecedented” circumstances for car stoppages on formation lap | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The FIA says an unexpected combination of factors caused the car stoppages which delayed the start of today’s race.

Multiple drivers encountered technical problems during the original attempt to start the race which followed the delay due to rain. Max Verstappen , Lewis Hamilton and others suffered a serious loss of power, causing their cars to slow and delay the rest of the pack.

Race control eventually abandoned the attempt to start the race and summoned the field back into the pits. The race finally started some 50 minutes later after software changes were applied to the cars.

The FIA confirmed the problem originated with its systems and said it would look into it.

“On the formation lap ahead of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit’s sector configuration led to an unintended loss of power for a number of cars,” it said in a statement.

“As a result, the FIA Technical Department removed the energy limit constraint in the affected sectors through an updated software release distributed to all competitors during the race delay caused by heavy rain enabling teams to make the necessary changes to the power unit before the start of the race.

“This issue had not been detected by the FIA or the teams during testing or during the laps to the grid. The FIA, together with the teams and power unit manufacturers, will undertake a full review of the issue.”

However Fernando Alonso claimed several drivers “stopped on the formation lap” and should not have been allowed to restart. “It’s the first time I see it,” he said. “I had half of the races this year with DNF and we never stopped the race. I hope they can do it next time we stop.”

Sports.title: “I guess it’s my fault” says Norris as stewards reprimand him for near-miss under Safety Car | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris admitted he was caught out by how quickly the field slowed ahead of him during the Safety Car period.

The McLaren driver almost ran into his team mate Oscar Piastri as they approached turn one in the queue behind the Safety Car. The incident occured as George Russell ahead of them slowed unexpectedly and came to a stop on the right-hand side of the track next to the pit lane entrance.

Norris said he noticed the Mercedes slowing but was unsure how much the cars ahead of him were reacting.

“I couldn’t see from the angle, and just from where I was, how much everyone had stopped because of George on the inside,” said Norris. “By the time I kind of looked at George and looked back, I could see them, but it’s hard when you’re directly behind to see if they’re going 100 [kph], 200 or 10.

“They were going 10, so I just got completely caught out. I guess it’s my fault in the end of the day. I was just unlucky with it everyone just checked up so much and I just got screwed over by it, that’s all.”

Norris narrowly missed hitting Piastri, ran onto the gravel trap on the outside then rejoined the queue having lost several places.

The stewards have summoned Norris for “driving erratically under Safety Car conditions, leaving the track and re-joining unsafely and/or overtaking another car behind the Safety Car.”

Alexander Albon is also under investigation for driving erratically in another incident which involved Piastri. The Williams driver, who was following his team mate Carlos Sainz Jnr into the pits during an earlier Safety Car deployment, appeared to slow, causing Piastri to take avoiding action.

Update: Norris has been reprimanded for his incident and Albon has been cleared.

Stewards’ verdict on Norris

While following the Safety Car, [Norris] approached turn one behind a group of cars. Car 63 (George Russell) had stopped with a mechanical problem ahead of turn one, which caused the cars ahead of Norris to slow down. Norris explained that, due to the low sun and resulting visibility conditions, it was difficult to recognise that the cars ahead had started to slow earlier than would normally have been expected. Norris consequently misjudged his closing speed and approached the cars ahead too quickly. When he realised this, he braked heavily and deliberately steered to the left, onto the kerbs and then into the gravel bed in order to avoid contact with the cars ahead. By driving onto the kerbs, Norris had reduced grip available for braking, which further limited his ability to slow the car. In doing so, Norris momentarily overshot car 81 (Oscar Piastri), who was directly ahead of him. The stewards considered whether this constituted an overtake while the Safety Car was deployed. Although Norris momentarily moved ahead of Piastri, this occurred solely as a consequence of Norris leaving the track while taking avoiding action. [Piastri] immediately repassed Norris while Norris was off the track. The stewards therefore determined that this did not constitute an overtaking manoeuvre and take no further action in respect of this aspect of the incident. The stewards also considered that, particularly while driving behind the Safety Car, Norris should have managed the gap to the cars ahead and his closing speed with greater care. The prevailing visibility conditions were circumstances which Norris should have taken into account when determining an appropriate speed and gap to the cars ahead, rather than a reason which excused the resulting driving. The need for heavy braking and an avoiding manoeuvre into the gravel demonstrated that Norris had not maintained an appropriate margin in the circumstances. The stewards therefore determined that Norris had driven erratically in breach of Article B5.13.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations. Such a situation should not arise while driving behind the Safety Car, and Norris was required to maintain a sufficient margin to the cars ahead. However, taking into account that Norris reacted promptly once he recognised the situation and successfully avoided contact, the stewards consider a reprimand as appropriate. The stewards separately considered Norris’s return to the track. Although car 18 (Lance Stroll) was in relative close proximity, Norris returned progressively and without requiring [Stroll] to take avoiding action or otherwise creating an unsafe situation. The stewards therefore determined that the re-join was safe. The stewards also reviewed whether, after having re-joined the track, Norris had overtaken Stroll while the Safety Car was deployed. The video evidence showed that, as Norris returned from the gravel, he had already crossed the white line with at least one wheel and, as such, was back on track. At this point, he was ahead of Stroll and at no point did Norris pass Stroll. Rather, Stroll approached Norris while Norris was already in the process of returning to the track. The stewards therefore determined that Norris had not overtaken Stroll under Safety Car conditions and as such also take no further action for this part of the incident. Accordingly, the stewards impose a reprimand on Norris for erratic driving. No further action is taken in relation to the re-join or the alleged overtake while the Safety Car was deployed.

Stewards’ verdict on Albon

On the approach to the pit entry, [Albon] reduced his speed, causing Piastri, who was following closely behind, to brake and take avoiding action. No collision or contact occurred. Albon explained that immediately before entering the pit entry road he became aware that he was below the required delta time and therefore reduced his speed in order to comply with the applicable delta requirement. Piastri confirmed, having heard Albon’s explanation, that he considered the reason for Albon’s actions understandable. While the situation required a significant reaction from Piastri and could potentially have developed into a dangerous situation, the stewards were satisfied that Albon’s actions were taken in an attempt to comply with the applicable delta requirements and explained the otherwise unusual reduction in speed at that location. His actions, therefore, did not constitute erratic or unnecessarily dangerous driving in the circumstances. Having considered the matter extensively, the stewards determine that no infringement occurred and accordingly take no further action.

Sports.title: Hadjar had “no battery” to defend from Hamilton and Leclerc in final laps | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar said he was unable to defend his podium position in the final laps of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The Red Bull driver held third place behind his team mate and Andrea Kimi Antonelli during the final Safety Car period. However he had both Ferraris close behind him.

Once the race restarted, Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc quick picked him off. Hadjar took the chequered flag in fifth place.

Hadjar successfully resisted Hamilton for many laps earlier in the race when his rival was on the medium tyre compound. However once Hamilton switched to soft tyres under the Safety Car, Hadjar fell prey to the Ferrari.

“I had no battery, something like that,” he explained. “So there was no contest against the Ferraris in the straight.”

However Hadjar was unhappy with his pace earlier in the race as well. “I don’t know what happened in terms of the grip I had on the car,” he said. “The whole race I was so slow.

“I don’t know what happened to my pace, but [it] really [was] one race to put in the bin.”

“We’ll fix the issue and understand why we are so bad today,” he added.

Sports.title: Wolff calls Mercedes’ Sepang race “one of my worst experiences” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff was deeply unhappy with their performance in today’s race.

The two W17s hit the front of the field immediately after the start. However Andrea Kimi Antonelli fell to second place behind Max Verstappen at the finish and George Russell retired shortly before the finish.

Antonelli increased his championship lead over Russell and Lewis Hamilton, though the latter recovered from a significant delay at the start of the race to salvage third place.

“I’m so massively annoyed and not in a happy place,” Wolff told Sky.

Mercedes introduced a significant upgrade for their car this weekend but appeared to gain little from it. “First of all, we didn’t have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend,” said Wolff. “So there’s a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I’m sure we will.

“Then the race literally went – if you consider the fight with Lewis behind – went against us. We had such an advantage. Two VSCs or one VSC, two safety cars. I mean, you couldn’t be more unlucky.”

Russell’s retirement – his third in a grand prix this season – leaves him 84 points behind Antonelli in the championship fight.

“To make things worse, a PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points,” Wolff continued. “So as much as I love to be here when I look at the pure races, one of my worst experiences to be honest.”

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker’s Showboating Gives Opponents Another Opening
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker’s showboating gave Conor Wallace opportunities to hit him after seemingly losing an exchange on Saturday night. Tony Bellew believes Whittaker has the talent to pull off those antics, but Wallace exposed what happens when an opponent keeps attacking instead of admiring them.

Whittaker would make Wallace miss or land a shot, then pause to showboat. Wallace pursued him and punched again. Making the first attack fail did not leave Whittaker safe from the next one, particularly when his attention shifted toward entertaining the crowd.

“You’re either good enough to do it, or you’re not. He is good enough to do it,” Bellew said on DAZN’s Beyond the Bell. “I don’t care if anyone’s a fan of it or you’re not. Are you good enough to pull this kind of stuff off? Are you good enough to try and be another Naseem Hamed? He is good enough.”

That defense overlooks the work Whittaker still needs to do after a successful exchange. He must leave punching range, recover his position, or stay ready to defend. Celebrating a slip or a landed punch gives a persistent opponent time to close the distance.

The same weakness appeared against Arlen Lopez in the Olympic final. Whittaker’s showboating did little to discourage the Cuban, who cut off the ring and landed punches. Against that kind of pressure, the extra movement becomes wasted energy when it fails to create a safer position or another scoring opportunity. Whittaker had nowhere to go because his feet were out of position from the routine.

Bellew described Whittaker’s late trouble against Wallace as switching off. Yet the showboating itself encourages those interruptions in concentration. An opponent does not have to accept that an exchange is finished simply because Whittaker starts performing.

Whittaker’s survival showed toughness, but it did not validate the antics that helped put him in danger. Wallace supplied a practical reason to shorten the performance between punches. Better opponents will keep working through it.

Prince Naseem Hamed had explosive, one-punch equalizer power that made opponents hesitant to rush him even when he clowned. Whittaker does not possess that kind of stopping power at light heavyweight. If he continues to pause for dramatic effect instead of completing his defensive recovery, world-class operators will time those mental lapses and put him on the floor.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Defends Against Oliver Zaren on Loaded Card
Sports.content:
Osleys Iglesias has the IBF super middleweight title, but the belt has yet to bring him the division’s biggest names. The Cuban puncher defends against Oliver Zaren this Thursday, October 8, on a Quebec City card featuring meaningful tests beneath the main event.

Iglesias (15-0, 14 KOs) puts his IBF and IBO belts on the line against unbeaten Danish challenger Zaren (19-0-1, 8 KOs) at Théâtre Capitole. The eight-fight Eye of the Tiger show airs on DAZN internationally and Punching Grace in Quebec, beginning at 6:30 p.m. ET.

His reputation as the division’s boogeyman has some evidence behind it. Canelo Alvarez and Jaime Munguia declined opportunities to face Iglesias for the vacant IBF title earlier this year, although Canelo cited recovery from elbow surgery. Those decisions left Iglesias seeking another opponent rather than securing a marquee fight.

Holding a championship gives Iglesias something to offer, but the commercial leverage still belongs to fighters with larger audiences. Facing an explosive southpaw brings considerable risk without necessarily producing a larger payday than a less dangerous opponent. Another stoppage could strengthen his reputation without making those negotiations easier.

Zaren deserves credit for accepting the challenge. His task is to interrupt Iglesias’ attacks and create room to work. Allowing the champion to dictate the pace would leave Zaren spending too much of the fight defending rather than building a winning performance.

The co-feature gives viewers a direct connection to Iglesias. Wilkens Mathieu (16-0, 11 KOs) defends his NABF super middleweight title against Vladimir Shishkin (17-2, 11 KOs), whom Iglesias stopped in September 2025. Their performances will invite comparison, although different styles make Shishkin an imperfect measuring stick. Mathieu still has to show he can handle an experienced contender.

At lightweight, Dzmitry Asanau (13-0, 7 KOs) faces Luis Santana (16-0, 7 KOs). Both belong to Eye of the Tiger, making this a welcome promotional risk. One prospect could lose his unbeaten record, but the winner gains evidence that he can defeat another developing contender.

Imam Khataev meets Padraig McCrory at light heavyweight, while Leila Beaudoin defends her interim WBA super featherweight title against Brisa Alfonzo.

The appeal extends beyond the nine belts being contested. Mathieu faces an experienced test, and Asanau and Santana must risk their unbeaten records. Iglesias supplies the knockout threat at the top while still chasing the opponents who could establish him as the best at 168.

Sports.title: Conah Walker and Alexis Rocha Agree Terms
Sports.content:
Conah Walker and Alexis Rocha have agreed to terms for a fight expected on December 5, bringing together two welterweights whose willingness to trade could produce a punishing night for both.

The attraction is easy to understand. Both are aggressive, hittable fighters who absorb punishment while trying to impose themselves. Whether that makes them suitable for a world title eliminator is a harder argument, although Eddie Hearn has yet to confirm that designation.

“We have agreed terms to fight Alexis Rocha,” Hearn said in the interview. “And that will be, looks like, December the 5th. So we’ll wait for an official announcement and what capacity that fight will be in. But I think it’s an absolute bloodbath, to be honest with you.”

Hearn was responding to a question about a report that Walker–Rocha could be a WBA eliminator. His answer confirmed progress on the matchup while leaving its championship implications unresolved.

As a fight, it has an obvious selling point. Neither man should need much encouragement to exchange, and their defensive shortcomings could give the other opportunities throughout. The danger is that an entertaining opening becomes a contest decided by who can withstand more damage.

For Walker, forcing exchanges could bring Rocha into the kind of physical fight he wants. However, walking forward also puts him within reach of Rocha’s combinations. Rocha would have opportunities to land, but staying close to follow up could leave him taking punches in return.

The possible eliminator label raises a separate issue. A competitive matchup between two willing sluggers does not automatically establish that either belongs near the front of the championship queue.

Welterweight’s thinner talent pool and multiple championship routes help explain how such an opportunity could emerge. With four major sanctioning bodies offering separate paths, fighters do not have to beat the same contenders to reach a title shot.

Walker–Rocha could deliver exactly the violence Hearn expects. Its entertainment value is easier to sell than its credentials as a gateway to a world championship.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker’s Next Fight Has Three Options
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn floated Conor Wallace, Anthony Yarde, and the winner of Joshua Buatsi against Willy Hutchinson as the potential next steps for Ben Whittaker. Taking the Wallace rematch makes the most sense because it directly answers the questions raised by that shaky finish in Birmingham last night.

Whittaker left with the decision, yet Wallace buzzed him in round ten, turning the final minutes into a desperate scramble to survive. Jumping immediately into a premier domestic clash invites serious danger before Whittaker proves he can fix those defensive holes.

“For me, no, he needs another fight. Now when I look at it, I think that’s the [Joshua] Buatsi-[Willy] Hutchinson winner, that’s [Anthony] Yarde, or it’s Conor Wallace,” Hearn said post-fight about Whittaker’s next opponent.

Wallace carries built-in drama for a second meeting. He knows he can rattle Whittaker, while Whittaker knows he can dominate the rounds when boxing on his terms. A return bout tests whether Wallace brings heat from the opening bell, and whether Whittaker maintains focus once under fire.

A basic points win changes little. Whittaker must command the championship rounds, clear his head instantly when tagged, and shut down sustained rallies after eating a clean shot.

Facing Joshua Buatsi or Willy Hutchinson is an immediate leap into danger. Both carry the thump and ring wisdom to punish defensive lapses, and neither will give away the opening half of a contest the way Wallace did. Even the loser of that matchup represents an unnecessary hazard.

Anthony Yarde offers an empty proposition. His name still resonates with British audiences, but stoppage losses to Artur Beterbiev and David Benavidez offer critics an easy asterisk. His heavy hands remain real enough to flatten Whittaker, leaving high physical risk without the sporting credibility to match.

That leaves Wallace as the most useful next opponent. Keeping the rematch in Birmingham could build on the first fight’s drama while giving Whittaker a familiar setting to show improvement.

A controlled twelve-round performance would provide stronger evidence for the next step up. Hearn has bigger names available, but Wallace has already supplied the test Whittaker needs to pass more convincingly.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Expects Los Angeles Meeting With Dana White
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn expects to meet Dana White in Los Angeles next week to discuss his involvement in Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua. Before agreeing to a role, Hearn wants to know what Joshua and Matchroom would receive in return.

That question gives the proposed meeting a purpose beyond settling their public argument. Hearn is leaving room for an agreement while using his claimed contractual veto to negotiate terms.

“What’s in it for Anthony? What’s in it for us?” Hearn said during his post-fight media session in Birmingham. “And once we establish that, we can make a decision. … They cannot be involved in the fight unless myself and Anthony allow them to be.”

Asked whether White would attend the Los Angeles meeting, Hearn said he was “supposed to be.” The meeting remains proposed rather than confirmed.

Hearn says Turki Alalshikh and Netflix want White involved. If his account of the contract is accurate, that gives Matchroom something to bargain with. Their preference for White doesn’t automatically supply a reason for Joshua’s side to accept him. Hearn could seek financial terms, promotional support or another concession, although he hasn’t disclosed any demands. His willingness to meet allows him to hear a proposal while keeping pressure on White to explain what he contributes.

The television production dispute adds another complication. Hearn claimed Sela had told him in writing that White’s statement about handling production was untrue. He maintained that the contract prohibits that involvement, although the relevant terms weren’t presented during the interview.

An appearance at a press conference and responsibility for producing the broadcast would involve different responsibilities. Any agreement would need to establish the scope of White’s role. Hearn also recognizes the promotional value of their rivalry. He acknowledged that the dispute has helped the buildup and said he wants to question White directly if they share a press conference stage.

That gives both sides a reason to find an arrangement. White could gain a visible role in the event, while their exchanges could attract further attention. Hearn’s position is that Joshua and Matchroom should receive a benefit for allowing it. The Los Angeles meeting could establish whether White’s side has an offer he considers worthwhile.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Revives Shakur Stevenson Fight Speculation
Sports.content:
Devin Haney’s Instagram promo featuring Shakur Stevenson puts a potentially lucrative matchup back into circulation as his inactivity approaches a year. Their stalled fight offers Haney a recognizable opponent, a winnable contest, and a way to regain attention after months on the sidelines.

Haney shared footage showing him facing off with Shakur, reviving speculation about their fight without confirming that negotiations have resumed. Devin’s side previously appeared willing to accept 144 pounds, but the fight never materialized. If talks restart, the camps would need to clarify whether Haney is still willing to fight at that weight.

The weight remains a potential obstacle. Haney would likely prefer 147 pounds, where he could face the smaller Shakur without cutting extra weight. Shakur previously wanted 144. Agreeing to that would mean Haney coming down three pounds, although we do not know whether the extra weight cut would weaken him.

😈😈😈😈😈 @Realdevinhaney LETS GO!!!! — Shakur Stevenson (@ShakurStevenson) October 4, 2026

Haney’s jab and reach give him a chance to beat Shakur without having to chase him. He can stay outside and make Shakur come forward to land punches. Both prefer opponents to attack first, so the fight could become cautious, with neither throwing much. Whoever lands his jab more consistently could win those close rounds.

Haney also needs to capitalize on his victory over Brian Norman Jr. from last November. Nearly eleven months have passed since he picked up the WBO welterweight belt. Crossing the November 22 mark without an opponent locked in burns an entire year of his prime. That kind of layoff wastes prime earning power, halts development inside the ropes, and chips away at fan interest.

Viable alternatives exist near 147 pounds if Shakur remains occupied with Gary Antuanne Russell. Richardson Hitchins, Liam Paro, Lewis Crocker, Teofimo Lopez, Jack Catterall, and Arnold Barboza Jr. all represent credible pairings, provided schedules cooperate. Haney has plenty of directions to turn, but he cannot afford to let another month slip by without putting a date on the calendar.

Shakur can pursue another title at 140 against Russell or revisit a potentially bigger payday against Haney. The Haney fight would require him to move up in weight against a larger opponent, making the catchweight agreement a major part of any renewed negotiations.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Calls Anthony Joshua A Usyk Warm-Up
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury is already looking past Anthony Joshua toward a trilogy bout with Oleksandr Usyk. He treats their December 11 Cardiff clash like tune-up work for a champion who already beat him twice.

That gives Joshua a golden opportunity to wreck everything. A loss completely ruins any market for another Usyk meeting, especially after Fury spent weeks dismissing Joshua as light work.

“I don’t have any intention of retiring after Joshua. I’m using this bum as a warm-up for Usyk,” Fury told Sky Sports.

Fury wants the Usyk trilogy in New York. He also points to his activity this year, including fights with Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach, as evidence that he will enter the Joshua bout ready.

Staying active helps Fury shake off ring rust, but Joshua brings threats none of those recent opponents offered. Joshua carries genuine power. Fury cannot afford to look past him or script future dates while dodging heavy artillery. A single defensive lapse ends all talk of a third Usyk clash instantly.

Joshua hits hard enough to test whether Fury still has elite reflexes over 12 rounds. Usyk is an entirely different animal. He relies on rapid footwork, awkward southpaw angles, non-stop punching. Fury could beat Joshua easily, but that does not solve the tactical problems that cost him against Usyk twice.

Winning in Cardiff gives Fury a huge name to brag about. It proves nothing about how a third fight with Usyk would turn out.

Fury’s trash talk is pure fight promotion. He degrades Joshua to sell the Cardiff gate while teasing an even bigger event down the line. His bravado sells tickets, but talk alone proves nothing about the reality inside his training camp.

If Fury wins, he could try to sell a big victory, but Usyk still holds two decisions over him. The champion would need serious motivation to face a boxer he conquered twice.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez Managers Meet
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez’s manager Keith Connolly has met with Ryan Garcia’s manager Lupe Valencia and teased a “mega fight.” However, making Garcia–Lopez could require Teofimo to give up his WBA welterweight title, with Jack Catterall’s mandatory defense due.

The money fight can happen without two belts. The question is whether Teofimo can take his WBA championship into it while Catterall insists on getting his opportunity.

“Met up with Lupe Valencia today in San Diego for coffee,” Connolly wrote on Instagram, in a screenshot shared by Dan Rafael. “Boxing fans get ready Mega Fight coming.”

Connolly did not identify the matchup or announce an agreement, but meeting with Ryan’s manager and posting that caption gives Garcia–Lopez speculation something more substantial than another exchange of callouts.

It does nothing to settle the Catterall situation.

Teofimo and Catterall have until October 22 to negotiate a deal for their WBA title fight before the organization can move toward a purse bid. Catterall has made clear he won’t step aside, leaving Teofimo’s team with an obligation that a separate agreement with Ryan would not erase.

Unless the WBA grants permission for Garcia–Lopez to go ahead first, Teofimo could have to sacrifice his belt to pursue it. The deadline itself would not automatically strip him, but signing for Ryan would still leave the mandatory unresolved.

From a business perspective, losing the WBA title might be a price Teofimo is willing to pay. Ryan offers a commercially attractive opponent, and his WBC championship would give Teofimo another title to chase if the fight proceeds as a sanctioned defense.

That would change the promotion from a welterweight unification to a challenge for Ryan’s belt, without necessarily reducing the fighters’ interest in making it.

Connolly’s post suggests there is something to watch. Until the Catterall obligation is addressed, though, the two-title billing remains uncertain.

Ghana News.title: The Paradox of Plenty — When every smartphone becomes a newsroom
Ghana News.content:
The newsroom is no longer the only place where a story can begin. Today, a smartphone, a microphone and the courage to ask questions can put an injustice before the entire nation and sometimes before the President himself.

There was a time when telling a national story required access to a newsroom, a television studio, a radio station, a printing press or a newspaper editor.

Today, that world has changed.

A smartphone with a camera, an internet connection and a social-media account can put an ordinary Ghanaian at the centre of a national conversation within minutes.

Welcome to the age of the citizen journalist, blogger and content creator.

And whether traditional journalists like it or not, these new voices are becoming an increasingly important part of Ghana's information ecosystem.

They are everywhere.

On busy streets. In marketplaces. At hospitals. In schools. At police stations. In communities where public officials rarely visit. At places where ordinary citizens feel ignored.

Sometimes, they arrive before the mainstream media.

Sometimes, they tell stories the mainstream media does not have the resources, time or editorial space to pursue.

And sometimes, they simply hold up a smartphone and ask a question that thousands or millions of Ghanaians have been waiting to ask.

That development deserves serious attention.

Ghana's media landscape has long been diverse, with private radio and television stations, online news platforms and state-owned media operating alongside one another. Reporters Without Borders describes Ghana as having a dynamic and diverse media environment and notes that the country's 1992 Constitution guarantees freedom of the press.

But the digital revolution has added an entirely new layer.

The phone has become a newsroom.

A Facebook Live broadcast can expose a problem.

A TikTok video can draw attention to an abandoned project.

A YouTube interview can give a struggling citizen an audience.

A blogger's post can force officials to respond.

And a short video recorded by an ordinary person can sometimes travel further than a carefully produced television report.

This is not necessarily a threat to journalism.

It can also be an opportunity.

Some content creators are helping people who previously had little access to powerful platforms to tell their stories. They are documenting alleged injustices, highlighting community problems and bringing issues to public attention.

Most importantly, they are sometimes helping citizens who feel that nobody is listening.

That is powerful.

And governments notice when citizens begin speaking directly to the public.

We have seen the Presidency respond publicly to claims circulating on social media. For example, in April 2026, President John Dramani Mahama directly addressed social-media claims about tricycles distributed under the Free Primary Healthcare Programme, explaining what the vehicles were intended for.

That example demonstrates something important: social media is no longer merely a place where people talk. It has become a place where public officials must sometimes answer.

But there is another side to this revolution.

With great communicative power comes great responsibility.

Not everyone holding a smartphone is a journalist.

Not every viral video is journalism.

Not every accusation is a fact.

And not every person who disagrees with a public official should be described as a victim of persecution.

The same freedom that allows a content creator to expose an injustice must also require that creator to exercise care with facts, allegations and people's reputations.

This is where the debate becomes complicated.

President Mahama and members of his government, like other public officials, can legitimately object to insults, personal attacks and abusive language directed at them and their families.

Criticism of government policy is one thing.

Calling out alleged wrongdoing is another.

But personal abuse, threats, deliberate falsehoods and degrading attacks are different matters.

We should be able to draw that line without destroying the fundamental principle of free expression.

Criticism is not the enemy of democracy.

Neither is responsible journalism.

The danger comes when criticism is answered with intimidation or when freedom of expression becomes an excuse for abuse.

The answer should therefore not be to silence Ghana's new digital voices.

The answer should be responsibility, evidence, accountability and the rule of law.

Where a content creator makes a serious allegation, let the evidence be examined.

Where a government official believes a law has been broken, let due process take its course.

Where a journalist or content creator is accused of an offence, let the courts determine the matter fairly.

And where a citizen raises a legitimate public-interest concern, the government should listen rather than dismiss the person simply because the message arrived through a smartphone.

That balance matters because Ghana's democracy depends not only on the right to speak but also on the public's ability to receive information and scrutinise those who exercise power.

Reporters Without Borders' 2026 assessment places Ghana 39th out of 180 countries in its World Press Freedom Index and describes Ghana as being in the “satisfactory” category, while also noting continuing concerns about attacks, obstruction and safety affecting journalists.

So, Ghana should protect the space for journalism, whether that journalism comes from a major television station, a newspaper newsroom, an online publication or a responsible citizen with a smartphone.

But the digital revolution must not become a licence for character assassination.

A blogger should be able to criticise a minister.

A content creator should be able to question the President.

A citizen should be able to document what appears to be an injustice.

But they should also be prepared to support serious claims with evidence and accept lawful accountability when they cross legal boundaries.

And government must exercise restraint.

Because when the state responds disproportionately to criticism, the message can become bigger than the original post.

The challenge before Ghana is therefore not whether citizen journalism should exist.

It is already here.

The real question is whether Ghana can build a digital public sphere where citizens can speak boldly, journalists can investigate freely, governments can be held accountable, and everyone, including the President, can be criticised without fear, while still respecting the law and the dignity of others.

The smartphone has given ordinary Ghanaians a voice.

That voice should not be abused.

But neither should it be unnecessarily silenced.

Let the citizen speak.

Let the journalist investigate.

Let the blogger question.

Let the content creator document.

And let the evidence, the law and the truth do the rest.

Because in today's Ghana, the next important national story may not begin inside a newsroom.

It may begin with someone standing on a roadside, holding a smartphone, saying:

“This is what is happening here. Somebody needs to listen.”

Ghana News.title: GTA sensitises taxi drivers in ‘Know Ghana’ tourism campaign
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Tourism Authority has begun sensitising taxi drivers to promote Ghana’s tourism attractions, culture and local experiences to visitors.

The first exercise was done with the Osu RE, Shoprite and Papaye drivers’ unions on Saturday, 3rd October 2026, as part of the Authority’s ‘Know Ghana’ campaign.

The campaign seeks to educate transport unions across the country on the Authority’s domestic marketing agenda, ‘See Ghana, Eat Ghana, Wear Ghana and Feel Ghana' as well as ‘Experience Ghana’.

The GTA says taxi drivers are important tourism ambassadors because, through their daily activities, they engage tourists and foreigners before, during and even after the ‘December in GH’ period.

The drivers were encouraged to provide visitors with useful information about Ghana’s tourist attractions, heritage, nightlife and cultural experiences.

They were also urged to engage tourists and introduce them to Ghana’s tourist sites, local cuisine, traditional and contemporary Ghanaian clothing, music, nightlife and other cultural experiences.

The sensitisation highlighted the importance of promoting Ghanaian music in their cars as part of Ghana’s cultural identity and tourism experience, particularly during the December in GH period.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority, Maame Efua Houadjeto, was represented by Kofi Atta Kakra Kusi, Deputy Director of Corporate Affairs; Francisca Boakye, Deputy Director of Corporate Affairs; Judith Kelly, Principal Corporate Affairs Officer; and Elvis Bruce Wallace, Greater Accra Chairman of the Tour Guides Association of Ghana (TORGAG).

The Authority believes that equipping taxi drivers with accurate and relevant information about Ghana’s tourism offerings will enable them to better assist tourists and encourage greater patronage of local tourism attractions, products and services.

The initiative forms part of broader efforts by the Ghana Tourism Authority to encourage both domestic and international visitors to explore, experience and support Ghana’s tourism and cultural heritage.

The GTA said the initiative is also intended to increase patronage of domestic tourism, boost the local economy, attract more tourist arrivals and receipts, including foreign exchange, and encourage investment in the economy.

Speaking to the media, Deputy Director of Corporate Affairs Kofi Atta Kakra Kusi reiterated the CEO’s call for similar exercises to be carried out at vantage taxi stations in Accra and across the 16 regions.

He said the exercise would also be extended to other transport unions, including GPRTU, Uber and Yango drivers.

Mr Kusi appealed to the media to give the exercise the needed publicity so that a wider audience could be reached to help promote and market Ghana’s tourism offerings.

As part of the sensitisation process, the team gave the drivers branded T-shirts, stickers and flyers for their cars to support the promotion and marketing of Ghana’s tourism offerings.

Ghana News.title: Archbishop Agyinasare calls for responsible speech amid growing social media abuse
Ghana News.content:
Archbishop Dr Charles Agyinasare, Founder and Leader of Perez Chapel International, has cautioned Ghanaians against normalising information disorder through the circulation of unverified allegations, threats and personal attacks on social media.

He also condemned the growing acceptance of abusive language and vulgarity in public discourse, saying citizens could demand accountability and expose corruption without attacking the dignity of others.

Archbishop Agyinasare gave the caution when he preached at a joint service to climax a week-long Breakthrough Conference in Accra on Sunday.

His sermon was on the theme: “Watch Your Words: The Power and Responsibility of Our Speech.”

“You can expose corruption without insulting people’s humanity,” he said, urging Ghanaians to uphold decency and mutual respect in their use of digital platforms.

He noted that the widespread use of smartphones and digital platforms had democratised broadcasting but had also increased the risk of spreading falsehoods, damaging reputations and deepening abusive public discourse.

The ease with which information could be published and shared, he said, placed a greater responsibility on users to verify facts before posting, commenting on or circulating content.

“We live in the age of the microphone,” he declared, adding that instant global reach came with the responsibility to ensure that information shared was truthful and responsible.

Archbishop Agyinasare warned that unverified claims circulated online could quickly gain traction and become accepted as truth if left unchallenged.

He urged Christians to ensure that their speech reflected their faith and advised social media users to apply a four-fold test before posting content: “Is it true? Have I established the facts? Is it gracious? Can I say it without humiliating someone?”

Drawing lessons from Matthew 13:35, Ephesians 5:4 and Colossians 4:6, Archbishop Agyinasare reminded believers that every person was created in the image of God and deserves to be treated with dignity, regardless of differences in opinion.

He urged Ghanaians to harness their digital influence responsibly by using their platforms to promote truth, elevate public discourse and contribute to a more respectful society.

Ghana News.title: ‘It will be inexcusable for gov’t not to honour payment of teachers’ arrears by 30th October’ – Haruna Iddrisu
Ghana News.content:
Haruna Iddrisu, the Minister of Education

Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu says the government will pursue supplementary payments for promoted teachers once the Ghana Education Service (GES) completes processing their details.

Speaking during a visit to GES staff working on the data on Sunday, October 4, Mr Iddrisu said the government expects the details of at least 51,000 promoted teachers to be ready for submission to the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD).

He said the completed data would enable the government to direct the Ministry of Finance to secure supplementary payment for the first phase.

“At least 51,000 would have been ready; then we can get and direct the Minister of Finance to get a supplementary payment for the first leg of it,” he said.

The Minister also assured teachers that the government’s commitment to settling their outstanding arrears must be honoured.

“It will be inexcusable for government not to honour the payment of the teachers’ promoted arrears by October 30th,” he added.

The GES has been given a 4 p.m. Monday, October 5 deadline to complete and submit the relevant details to the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department.

GES Director-General Prof Ernest Kofi Davis told JoyNews on Sunday that officials were working with the Controller’s team to reconcile the data.

He said the Service was targeting between 51,000 and 52,000 promoted teachers and was doing everything possible to meet the deadline.

The teacher unions – the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG) – have cited delayed promotions and the payment of outstanding arrears among their concerns in the ongoing industrial action.

Ghana News.title: Forbes’ World’s Best Employers 2026: No Ghanaian firm ranked among 900 companies
Ghana News.content:
No Ghanaian firm was ranked among the 900 firms in Forbes’ World’s Best Employers 2026 rankings.

Most of the Africa-ranked firms were from South Africa, Nigeria and Egypt.

Nine of the top 10 firms came from South Africa, with subsidiaries in Ghana. They include Standard Bank (Stanbic), Absa, First National Bank, MTN and Sanlam Insurance.

Guaranty Trust Bank (277) was the only firm from Nigeria in the top 10, though Access Bank placed 704.

South Africa's dominance is noticeable in the ranking.

Nedbank led the continent at number 26 globally. Standard Bank Group followed at number 54, while Absa Group and FirstRand placed 98th and 104th, respectively.

Six of the top 10 firms were from the banking and financial services industries.

Microsoft was the best-ranked firm from the United States of America. It was followed by Delta Airlines and Shopify from the USA and Canada, respectively.

Other best-ranked top 10 firms were Costco (USA), NVIDIA (USA), Adobe (USA), Apple (USA), Sony (Japan), Alphabet (USA) and Lego Group (Denmark).

The survey covered multinational companies with more than 1,000 employees, while the final 2026 list features 900 companies headquartered across 52 countries.

Employees assessed their employers on several aspects of the workplace, including how likely they were to recommend their company to family and friends, as well as benefits, talent development, work environment and training opportunities.

Respondents could also rate former employers they had worked for within the previous two years and companies they knew through their industry or personal networks.

The methodology therefore provides a snapshot of employee perceptions of large, internationally active employers rather than a broad assessment of workplace culture across Africa.

Ghana News.title: Electronic processing of teachers’ data: ‘The decision is the Controller’s’ – GES boss
Ghana News.content:
Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES), Prof Ernest Kofi Davis, says he would prefer the details of promoted teachers to be processed electronically, but the final decision rests with the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD).

Prof Davis said the GES only facilitates the process and does not have the authority to determine how the information is processed by the department responsible for payment.

“That is my wish, but the answer is the Controller’s. That is outside our remit. We don’t pay. We only facilitate the process. So the decision is the Controller’s. But that is my wish,” he said.

He was speaking as GES officials worked to process the details of promoted teachers for submission to the CAGD, amid efforts to resolve issues linked to the ongoing teachers’ strike.

Asked whether the process could be moved to an electronic system, Prof Davis said it was possible but stressed that the CAGD would have to make the final decision.

“It should be possible, but then as I said, the decision is the Controller’s. But I wish we could go to the system,” he said.

Prof Davis said the large volume of paperwork involved in the exercise highlighted the need to consider a more modern approach to handling teachers’ records.

“You can see the stash of papers around. You get bags in the 21st century. I don’t know whether that is the way we want to go, but the decision is the Controller’s,” he said.

The GES is also working to meet a 4 p.m. Monday deadline to complete and submit the details of thousands of promoted teachers to the CAGD.

The deadline was set by Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu as part of efforts to address concerns over delayed promotion placements and arrears, which are among the issues behind the ongoing nationwide strike by pre-tertiary teacher unions.

Ghana News.title: Teachers’ Strike: Haruna Iddrisu questions paper-based processing of promoted teachers’ data
Ghana News.content:
Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has questioned the continued use of paper forms to process the details of promoted teachers, calling for an electronic system to make the process more efficient.

Mr Iddrisu raised the concern during a visit to Ghana Education Service (GES) staff working to compile and process data on promoted teachers for submission to the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD).

The exercise forms part of efforts to complete the processing of teachers’ promotion details, a key step towards addressing concerns linked to the ongoing nationwide teachers’ strike.

Mr Iddrisu said the process should be modernised and supported by an information technology system rather than relying on teachers and officials to handle large volumes of paperwork.

“We must find a way of doing this better than we are doing. Why are we doing that? Why should teachers at this age be filling forms?” he asked.

He said the use of technology would provide a more efficient way of handling the information and reduce the burden associated with the current process.

“The only way we can do so is using an IT infrastructure system,” the Minister said.

He added that he would raise the issue with the relevant authorities and push for a better system to be adopted in future.

“I’ll raise questions about this and I think that we must find a better way of doing it than this manner,” he said.

The Minister also expressed concern about the volume of paper and other materials being handled by officials working on the exercise.

“But how can we carry all this material? How can we carry all this?” he asked.

“We cannot be filling forms by this age,” he added.

Mr Iddrisu’s comments came as GES staff worked to meet a 4 p.m. Monday deadline to process the details of promoted teachers for submission to CAGD.

The submission is an important step towards having the affected teachers’ promotion details captured and processed.

The exercise has taken on added significance amid the ongoing teachers’ strike, with the government working to address issues at the centre of the industrial action.

Ghana News.title: Savannah Region: Kunfusi bridge collapses again, leaving nearly 4,000 residents cut off
Ghana News.content:
About 4,000 residents in the Sawla-Tuna-Kalba District of the Savannah Region are facing difficulties reaching health facilities and markets after the Kunfusi Bridge collapsed for the second time.

The collapse, reported on October 4, 2026, followed several days of heavy rainfall, disrupting travel along a route linking Kunfusi with Kalba, Tuna and other communities. The bridge also serves travellers heading towards Burkina Faso and Côte d’Ivoire.

Residents say the damage has restricted access to essential services and made it difficult for farmers to transport their produce to market.

Volunteers have been helping pedestrians and motorists negotiate the damaged crossing while appealing for urgent action to restore access.

The Assembly Member for the Kunfusi Electoral Area also called for immediate intervention, highlighting the difficulties confronting affected communities.

Savannah Regional Minister Salisu Bia Wurbe visited the site with officials from the Regional Coordinating Council and the Sawla-Tuna-Kalba District Chief Executive to assess the damage.

Addressing the media after the inspection, the Minister said the collapse had affected access to healthcare and other essential services for a significant number of people in the district.

He indicated that efforts would be made to reconnect the affected communities while arrangements for a new bridge were pursued.

Mr Bia Wurbe urged residents to avoid the damaged crossing because of the danger it posed and to use alternative routes where available.

Residents are calling for a swift response to ease the disruption and restore reliable access to health facilities, markets and neighbouring communities.
