World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Ireland refuse handshake with Israel and don armbands in Nations League tie
World.content:
Republic of Ireland football players again wear black armbands and refuse handshakes with Israel in UEFA Nations League.

Ireland players again wore black armbands in recognition of Palestinians killed in Gaza and bowed their heads during the Israeli national anthem before the teams’ second UEFA Nations League football match on Sunday.

The League 3 Group B match ended in a 1-1 draw and, despite being played behind closed doors and on neutral ground, was once again played out in a confrontational manner.

Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher stepped in as captain for Dara O’Shea, who was excused to be with his wife for the birth of their child, and pointedly avoided shaking hands with Israel captain Dor Peretz, despite completing the usual pre-match formality with the referee and one of his assistants.

Kelleher’s action was a repeat of O’Shea’s, who refused to shake Israel captain Manor Solomon’s hand before the first match in Debrecen, Hungary, last week. Ireland went on to win that game 3-0 through three first-half goals.

Solomon was dropped to the bench for Sunday’s match in Backa Topola, Serbia. Israel forward Sayed Abu Farchi was back in the squad after serving a suspension for getting sent off following his gun-simulation goal celebration during Israel’s 3-1 defeat to Austria on September 25.

Finn Azaz, whose mother has Israeli heritage, was among the Irish substitutes after playing from the start against Austria on Thursday.

Troy Parrott’s penalty in the 39th minute, after a foul by Peretz on Jimmy Dunne, gave Ireland a 1-0 halftime lead. A disagreement also broke out on the sidelines as the players made their way off the field for the interval, although the referee quickly intervened.



Peretz secured a point for Israel with a poked effort from close range in the 47th minute.

Sunday’s game was initially supposed to be played in Dublin, but the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) moved it to a neutral venue for “operational reasons” in June following widespread calls for a boycott in protest of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. The FAI said the game would be played with no fans present.

It followed the FAI’s motion the previous November calling on UEFA to ban Israel from club and international competitions.

All the Irish players had been under pressure from home – where affinity with Palestinians is strong – to boycott the second match against Israel, though the pressure was greater during the first game.

“I felt that pressure growing day by day, and it’s getting almost to a breaking limit now,” Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said at the time.

Ultimately, only reserve goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu decided to skip both of the contentious games, saying in a statement that it was his “personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong”.

More than 160 Irish sportspeople had signed an open letter urging the FAI to reconsider its decision to go ahead with the two games.

Before the departure for Hungary, people protested outside the team hotel in Dublin for the players to boycott the matches. The SIPTU trade union displayed a huge poster in central Dublin beside the River Liffey asking the players to “Go with your conscience!” and “Don’t play with genocide” beside an image of a blood-splattered ball.

Former Ireland coach Brian Kerr said the FAI had “lost the respect of the Irish people” for going ahead with the games.

But the FAI argued UEFA could sanction the team. Ireland is cohosting the 2028 European Championship with England, Wales and Scotland.

Protesters threw tennis balls with Palestinian flags onto the field during Ireland’s 2-2 draw with Austria on Thursday. A man with a Palestinian flag also tried running onto the field.

On Saturday, an Israeli journalist stated during the pre-match news conference that the Irish players had called the Israeli players “monkeys” during last week’s game, leading to an immediate rebuke from Irish communications officer Kieran Crowley, who said it was “a lie” and ended the news conference.

The players had only decided to go ahead with the fixtures after a dramatic day in Debrecen before the first match, when both the news conference and training were delayed for hours while they deliberated. They reportedly voted 14-8 in favour of continuing after Bazunu’s withdrawal that morning.



Ireland’s national broadcaster RTÉ was only providing stripped-back coverage of both games against Israel to meet contractual obligations. There was no studio presentation, commentary on the international feed, or analysis. RTÉ said it was not accepting advertising or sponsorship around either game.

RTÉ also recently announced that Ireland will boycott the Eurovision Song Contest for a second year due to Israel’s participation.

World.title: Ronaldo-less Portugal beat Norway 2-1 to reach Nations League quarterfinals
World.content:
Holders Portugal first team to qualify for 2026-27 UEFA Nations League despite Cristiano Ronaldo’s absence.

Portugal defeated Norway 2-1 on Sunday, without superstar striker Cristiano Ronaldo, to qualify for the UEFA Nations League quarterfinals.

Goncalo Ramos secured victory for Jorge Jesus’s Portugal in the Group A4 clash after Joao Cancelo’s rocket levelled Kristoffer Ajer’s stunning opener for Norway.

Portugal played out the final minutes with 10 men after Francisco Conceicao was dismissed for two yellow cards in the space of a few seconds for dissent following his unsuccesful appeal for a penalty.

Former Real Madrid and Manchester United striker Ronaldo walked out on the squad on Wednesday, ahead of the previous game against Denmark, after Portugal’s all-time top goalscorer learned he would not start.

Portugal are now guaranteed to finish in the top two spots in the group, thus granting them passage to the last eight in March 2027.

Norway took the lead in Porto against the run of play with a stunning effort from Brentford defender Ajer after 36 minutes.

The Norwegian met a bouncing ball on the edge of the box perfectly and bent it into the top corner.

However, two minutes later, Barcelona defender Cancelo scored a similarly superb goal, rifling home from about 20 yards.

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland fired across the face of goal after an hour and was replaced by Jorgen Strand Larsen a few minutes later.

Nations League holders and two-time record champions Portugal nosed in front when AC Milan striker Ramos, starting in place of Ronaldo, tucked home from close range after being teed up by Joao Felix.



Conceicao’s foolish dismissal left Jesus’s team in a tough spot for the final few minutes, but they held on to triumph for the fourth time in four games in the group.

World.title: Israel lashes out as UK’s Green Party formally defines Zionism as ‘racism’
World.content:
Share Israel lashes out as UK’s Green Party formally defines Zionism as ‘racism’ on social media

Israel has reacted with anger after the United Kingdom’s Green Party voted to define Zionism as a form of racism.

Israel, as well as British Jewish groups, lashed out on Sunday following the vote by the small political party. The Israeli government declared that it now views the left-leaning Greens as giving “legitimacy to terrorism”.

The Green Party, which received 6 percent of the vote in the UK’s national elections in 2024, said ⁠it regarded Zionism as “an ethnonationalist political project” and repeated its call for Britain’s Labour government to end all arms trade with Israel.

In a swift response, Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the policy went “far beyond the boundaries of legitimate political debate” and called on other British political parties to condemn the resolution.

“The Greens have adopted not only the green of Hamas, but also its ideology: the elimination of the State of Israel through armed struggle,” the ministry wrote on social media.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog labelled the move “a disgrace and a shame”. Writing on social media, he said: “Those who claim the antisemitic lie that ‘Zionism is racism’ deliberately endanger Jews and Israelis everywhere.”

Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid said it is “not Zionism that’s racism, it is the Green Party”.

The Movement for Progressive Judaism, a British group, said: “The Green Party has made ⁠antisemitism party policy and become a racist party”.

It added that the support of some Jews for the motion did not mean it would not be used to discriminate against others.

During the vote, the Green Party also reaffirmed its “commitment to Palestinian liberation, the right of return, Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS), and a full arms embargo against Israel”.



It also reiterated support for “the establishment of a single democratic state throughout historic Palestine”, the party said in a statement.

The motion was backed by a majority of 1,022 to 813. Party leader Zack Polanski, who is running for Parliament in former Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s London constituency, did not vote.

In an interview with UK media outlet Sky News, the Greens’ co-deputy leader Mothin Ali said that the heavy casualty toll during Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza and its ongoing attacks were the context for the vote.

The Green Party has five sitting members in the UK’s 650-seat parliament.

Following the passage of the resolution, Polanski and other Green Party members said in a joint statement they would “continue to stand in opposition to genocide, ethnic cleansing, apartheid and the illegal occupation” and “call out the heinous crimes of the Netanyahu government”.

World.title: Will elections bring change to multi-ethnic Bosnia and Herzegovina?
World.content:
Balkan nation seeks EU membership, but divisions threaten that goal.

Voters in Bosnia and Herzegovina go to the polls for the 10th time since the end of the war more than three decades ago.

They’re electing more than 500 members of a complex government structure.

The Dayton Peace Accord ended the war in 1995.

But deep political and ethnic divides remain.

Some analysts say this vote could be the most consequential since the agreement was signed.

So, how will it play out, both in Bosnia and in the region?

Presenter: Sami Zeidan

Guests:

Jahja Muhasilovic – Assistant Professor at the International University of Sarajevo

Nina Sajic – Professor in the School of Political Science at the University of Banja Luka

Bodo Weber – Senior Associate at the Democratization Policy Council

World.title: France to shutter up to 500 schools as more student protests called
World.content:
French education minister cites safety concerns for closures as resumption of protests are called for by organisers.

Share France to shutter up to 500 schools as more student protests called on social media

France plans to fully or partially close up to 500 schools on Monday amid a series of student protests that have become increasingly violent.

Education Minister Edouard Geffray announced the precautionary measures on Sunday as part of a bid for a “partial, progressive return to lessons”. However, after a weekend lull, student protestors announced they plan to resume demonstrations – launched last month over complaints regarding class sizes, lack of teachers, and other complaints – early in the week.

Lessons will be “totally or partly suspended” in some “400-500” high schools as the security conditions “have not been fulfilled”, the minister said. He added that 24 schools had been “burned or ransacked” since the start of the protests.

Geffray said the closures were a security precaution. Protest organisers have called for a return to large-scale demonstrations on Tuesday, citing a lack of “concrete measures” from President Emmanuel Macron’s government.

At least 170 students and 78 educational personnel have been injured since the student demos first erupted in the Paris region in mid-September, according to Geffray.

The Ministry of National Education reported that at least 400 of the 3,700 high schools in France were closed on Friday, while 560 faced protests or disruptions.

The number of schools affected on Monday would be comparable to the figure from Friday, Geffray said.



Teachers and students first mobilised at a high school in a Paris suburb on 17 September over a lack of teaching staff, excessive school-day hours and other grievances. The protests have since spread nationwide, resulting in class strikes, blockades and demonstrations.

According to the interior minister, more than 5,000 people have been arrested in the last week; 85 percent of them minors.

Critics have criticised “disproportionate” police violence in response to the demonstrations. Rights group Amnesty International said the student protestors “must be listened to, not repressed”.

In an interview on French public radio, Geffray claimed far-left activists “infiltrated the high school student movement, hijacked it from the students themselves and engaged in extreme violence.”

World.title: Pro-Imran Khan mass rally launched after Pakistan government talks fail
World.content:
Government warns of crackdown as supporters of jailed former prime set off from northwest Pakistan towards Islamabad.

Supporters of jailed former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan have set off on a protest march from the country’s northwest after talks with the government to call off the demonstration failed.

More than 5,000 were reported to have begun the rally on Sunday. The march, planned by Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party, was originally scheduled for September 27 but was postponed until October 4 to allow talks between the government and the PTI leadership to take place.

However, two rounds of talks over the weekend failed to break the deadlock, and the PTI decided to carry out its plan, which is the latest attempt to pressure the government into releasing Khan, the country’s most popular political figure according to polls, who has been behind bars since August 2023 following a series of convictions that his party calls politically motivated.

All but one of the convictions against the former PM have since been suspended or overturned on appeal.

Videos posted on the PTI’s official social media showed supporters joining the march in different areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province, which is ruled by the party, and setting off in convoys.

Sohail Afridi, the region’s chief minister, had earlier posted on social media that the demonstration in support of Khan would go ahead.

He said the march will make its way to Khairabad, 80 kilometres (50 miles) west of Islamabad, by Thursday, where the plan for the “next phase” will be announced.

Government warns protesters

The government has been preparing for weeks for the arrival of PTI demonstrators in Islamabad. It has erected barriers using shipping containers to block main access routes to the capital.



Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi confirmed earlier on Sunday that the talks between the two sides had failed. He accused Afridi of “sabotaging” the negotiations, and added that the government would not allow the PTI to “create a disturbance”.

He also cited an Islamabad High Court order from September 14, ruling that no political party or its leadership has the “lawful right to occupy public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas and buildings in Islamabad”.

“If they violate the orders, whether they are workers or politicians, whether they are protesting within KP or outside KP, we will pursue them one by one. This time, we want to ensure that these repeated episodes of creating disturbance in Islamabad come to an end,” Naqvi said.

Concerns about the 73-year-old Khan’s health, in particular the condition of his right eye that has required months of specialist treatment, have prompted the PTI’s campaign for his release.

The party has also called for the release of Khan’s three sisters, whose arrests last month further heightened tensions.

James Dorsey, a fellow at the National University of Singapore, said Khan was “essentially a populist leader” with “a genuine popular movement that had broad popular support”.

That is behind the “determination by the government to prevent [the protesters] from entering Islamabad,” he told the AFP news agency.

Given Pakistan’s security concerns, particularly following its unresolved February 2026 conflict with Afghanistan, Islamabad wants to avoid escalation in the face of the protests, he added.

“It’s a problem for the government, but I don’t think it’s an existential threat,” he said.

World.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
World.content:
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two people were injured in the latest Russian attack. He earlier said that the Pivnichnyi Bridge's roadway was hit.

Kyiv's eight bridges across the wide Dnipro River link the western (right) and eastern (left) parts, and many of the capital's estimated three million residents rely heavily on the metro lines and trains to travel across the city.

Some 500,000 vehicles use the bridges every day.

The two struck bridges are still standing - but the damage and restrictions to traffic and public transport have caused gridlock in parts of the capital at times.

"To get from the left bank to the right one and back - it's just hell," Kyiv resident Roman told the BBC on Sunday.

Large numbers of commuters cross the river, especially on weekdays. Repair teams are working to fix the damage and officials say they are planning temporary pontoon bridges, ferry services and even a tunnel under the river to keep Kyiv connected.

Klitschko also said a separate Russian drone strike had damaged a heating main, adding that there would be a temporary lack of hot water in the north-eastern Desnyanskyi district as a result.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenksy said on Sunday morning Russian drones had also attacked a warehouse in the north-eastern region of Sumy, killing one person.

Meanwhile, in the central city of Dnipro, six people were injured after a communications facility was struck, he said.

Ukraine's Air Force said that overnight Russia had launched 135 drones, including 52 jet-powered ones. It said that 125 projectiles had been shot down.

World.title: Watch: What we know about Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges
World.content:
Major bridges in Ukraine have been the target of Russian strikes over the past four days, as Moscow ramps up attacks in Ukraine's capital city.

The Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, has been hit for the second day in a row, while the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times earlier this week.

The latest attack came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a visit to Kyiv on Sunday.

BBC Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson is near one of the bridges that was targeted and explains what we know so far.

World.title: Yemen's government announces all-out war to reclaim land from Houthis
World.content:
The head of Yemen's internationally recognised government has announced it will wage an all out war in an effort to take all territory held by the Houthis.

It follows an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in recent days.

The Iran-backed group said it had struck sites belonging to Saudi national oil company Aramco, in response to what it described as 50 Saudi-led coalition strikes in 12 hours. Saudi Arabia has yet to comment.

The Yemeni government's fierce statement was expected after the Houthis' offensive last month, which saw them seize control of the country's coastline, including the vital shipping lane of the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

World.title: Polls close in Brazil as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro remain neck and neck
World.content:
Polls have closed in Brazil's general election, after voters queued in long lines for a tight first round of the presidential race.

After casting his ballot, 80-year-old left-wing President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva warned that the choice was between democracy and "barbarism".

His challenger, right-winger FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, 45, said he wanted to "free the Brazilian people".

The result is forecast to be close. BBC Brazil's poll aggregator shows that the gap between Lula and Bolsonaro is only two points. If no candidate gets more than 50% of the vote, the election will go to a run-off on 25 October.

According to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE), more than 158.7 million Brazilians, including one million people abroad, are eligible to vote in the election.

Lula is challenged by 11 candidates, although BBC Brazil's poll aggregator shows that candidates other than Lula and Bolsonaro will get only about 10% of the vote.

The TSE has not set a fixed time for the release of the official results, but they are expected within hours because voting is electronic and experience from previous elections shows that results tend to come quickly.

A victory for Bolsonaro would extend a wave of wins across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with US President Donald Trump, while Lula's re-election would create problems for Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security.

World.title: Ethiopian rebel forces withdraw from Tigray regional capital
World.content:
Rebel forces in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region have said they have temporarily withdrawn from the regional capital, Mekelle, as fighting with the national army moves towards the city.

The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which has been running the region, said its decision to relocate was made because of concerns about risks to civilians.

Two residents in Mekelle told the BBC that pro-government forces now control the city and TPLF forces have abandoned it. One resident also said mobile phone services appear to have resumed in parts of the city.

Fighting has erupted in recent weeks between the TPLF and federal government forces alongside allied fighters in parts of Ethiopia's northern regions of Tigray, Afar and Amhara.

The development marks a major shift in the conflict and raises concerns among observers that the fighting could further destabilise the Horn of Africa, potentially drawing in neighbouring countries.

The US Department of State called for "restraint" and "dialogue" on all sides ahead of a diplomatic meeting about the conflict in Egypt on Sunday with leaders from some of Ethiopia's neighbours.

World.title: Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says
World.content:
US murderer Christa Pike remains critically ill in hospital and her prognosis is still unclear following her failed execution, her lawyer has said on Sunday.

Speaking to CNN on Sunday morning, Pike's lawyer Stephen Ferrell said doctors were still trying to clear two doses of pentobarbital from her body.

Pike, 50, was sentenced to death following her conviction for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995.

She survived two execution attempts on Wednesday, and was transferred to a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee.

Ferrell said: "She's still in the hospital, on a ventilator, critically ill, we really don't know the prognosis yet, and may not know for several days."

He didn't believe she had regained consciousness at any point, adding that he has been receiving updates through her medical power of attorney rather than consulting directly with doctors.

He has not been in to see her. "She is guarded. I'm not sure who may have seen her," he said.

Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. But Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year - and the head of prisons in the state said he would resign on Saturday.

"If she recovers - she may not fully recover - and there may be issues about her competence. I mean, we just don't know any of this," Ferrell said. "We have had no discussions about this. The Tennessee attorney general's office so far has not given us any indications of what their intentions will be."

World.title: Indian police accused of sexually harassing journalists at protest
World.content:
Three female journalists have accused police officers in India of sexual harassment during street protests in the capital Delhi.

The claims were made on Saturday after the force detained scores of young people calling for the resignation of the chief election commissioner.

In a post on social media, Delhi Police said its New Delhi District had received the complaint, and it had been transferred to its crime branch for a "fair and impartial" inquiry.

Thousands of protesters gathered in Delhi and Mumbai cities for a third day on Sunday demanding that Gyanesh Kumar step down over large-scale changes to voter rolls.

The Election Commission says the exercise is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible entries - and so far, 130 million names have been struck off the voters' list.

Videos online show people being physically dragged away from the Jantar Mantar protest site in central Delhi.

The accusations by the women journalists include inappropriate touching by some police.

Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi said women fear for their safety and the home ministry must "answer for this".

"Police dragged me by my hair," Aahna Singh, an activist and student at Jawaharlal Nehru University told Reuters news agency during the protests.

She said the police were resorting to "brutality".

The Press Club of India has demanded immediate action on the complaints against police officers, saying it was "shocked and dismayed" by the treatment of journalists.

"Behaviour of this kind cannot be normalised in a democracy. Journalists must be allowed to work freely, without fear, and document those who gather to raise various issues," it said in a statement.

World.title: US Marine arrested over murder of woman in Okinawa, Japan
World.content:
A US Marine has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a woman's body was found in a hotel in Okinawa, Japan, local officials say.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described the crime as a "brutal and heinous" robbery and murder. She said she had urged the US to "enforce stricter discipline" of its personnel.

Japan's public broadcaster NHK identified the victim as Yagi Anna, 39, and the suspect as Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who is stationed at US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma.

"We are actively cooperating with Japanese authorities, in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine," the Marine Corps said on social media, extending condolences to the victim's family.

Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said the woman's body was discovered early Saturday morning in a hotel in Naha City, the capital of the Okinawa prefecture.

"Such an incident is utterly inexcusable and fills me with strong indignation," Koizumi wrote on social media, adding that "incidents and accidents involving U.S. military personnel cause significant anxiety to the local community and must never occur".

The US Embassy in Tokyo said that it was fully cooperating with the Japanese government and local police. Japan's foreign ministry said it summoned US ambassador George Glass to discuss the incident on Sunday.

Okinawa is home to several US military bases and tens of thousands of American troops.

Okinawa Governor Genta Koja says the prefecture has repeatedly demanded that the US take action to prevent such incidents, and said he sees the alleged crime as a sign of a lack of discipline.

"The fact that this kind of event has happened again leaves us no choice but to conclude that the US military's efforts in maintaining discipline, educating personnel, and other such measures are completely ineffective," he said.

World.title: Police rescue kidnap victim, arrest suspected cultists
World.content:
The police in Delta State have rescued a kidnapped woman and arrested five suspects in separate operations in the state.

The police spokesperson in the state, Bright Edafe, disclosed this in a statement sent to PREMIUM TIMES on Sunday.

Mr Edafe, a superintendent of police, said the operations also led to the recovery of several items, including a fabricated Beretta pistol, a magazine, two rounds of live ammunition, a battle axe, four cutlasses and a hammer.

Kidnapped woman rescued

The police said operatives of the Otu-Jeremi Division rescued a 25-year-old woman who was allegedly assaulted and held hostage at Usiefrun Community.

The rescue operation was carried out on Saturday following intelligence shared by the Divisional Police Officer of the Ovwian-Aladja Division, the statement said.

A 29-year-old man, Brotugbare Onome, was arrested in connection with the incident.

A search of the premises where the woman was rescued led to the recovery of a fabricated Beretta pistol, one magazine and two rounds of live ammunition, according to the police.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Two arrested over alleged cult killing

In a separate incident, operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU) arrested two suspected cultists over the alleged killing of a 25-year-old man identified as Godfrey.

The police said Godfrey was allegedly killed at Jesse Main Market in Ethiope West Local Government Area on 24 March.

The arrests followed intelligence allegedly obtained from a viral video showing suspected cultists celebrating the killing.

PREMIUM TIMES has not seen the video.

The VCRU operatives, acting on the intelligence, raided a suspected criminal hideout in Oghara on 1 October.

The operation led to the arrest of Ezekiel Izomor, 23, and Emmanuel Ogaganefe, 23, the police said.

A battle axe, four cutlasses and a hammer were recovered during the operation, according to the statement.

The police said, “Preliminary investigation indicated that a suspect identified as Collins allegedly wanted to become the leader of the Aro Bagger confraternity and believed that killing a rival cult member would help him secure the leadership position.”

The police said Collins allegedly connived with Mr Izomor, Mr Ogaganefe and another suspect identified as Richman, who was a close friend of the deceased.

“Richman and Collins are at large, but efforts to arrest them is on top gear,” Mr Edafe said.

Two arrested over alleged kidnap plot

In another separate incident, the police arrested two men over an alleged plot to kidnap a woman in Abraka.

The police identified the suspects as Endurance Akpade, 37, and Edwin Morgan, 43.

The suspects, the police said, remain in custody and are assisting with the investigation.

The latest operations come amid increased police action against cultism and drug-related crimes in Delta State.

The command recently announced the arrest of a suspected drug peddler and the recovery of illicit drugs in another operation.

In a separate operation, the police said they raided a suspected drug spot, arrested suspects and recovered firearms.

The Commissioner of Police in the state, Samuel Erale, commended the officers involved in the operations.

Mr Erale urged residents to provide credible and timely information to the police to assist efforts against kidnapping, cultism and other violent crimes.

He also warned youths against cultism, saying the practice could destroy their future.

World.title: Vice Chancellor speaks on Anthony Kila’s fake professorship
World.content:
The Vice-Chancellor of the Michael and Cecilia Ibru University , Delta State, Ibiyinka Fuwape, has said his institution would soon respond to questions arising from a PREMIUM TIMES investigation that found no evidence to support claims by its pro-chancellor, Anthony Kila, that he is a professor.

The investigation, published on Saturday morning, examined Mr Kila’s academic credentials and found that contrary to his claims, he does not hold the rank of professor and was never so confirmed by any university.

More than 24 hours after the publication, however, the university has yet to issue a public statement on the findings or clarify its position regarding Mr Kila’s designation.

PREMIUM TIMES made repeated attempts to obtain the institution’s reaction.

A telephone line listed on the university’s website for general enquiries did not connect. One number identified as belonging to the registry rang without being answered, while another registry contact was answered by a person who said the line was private and had no connection with the university.

The newspaper eventually reached the university’s Vice-Chancellor and Professor of Physics, Ibiyinka Fuwape, who said the institution would respond after internal consultations.

“We will reply you very soon. The PRO will get in touch with you. The council is yet to meet. I can’t give you any information other than that,” Ms Fuwape said.

Asked when the public should expect a response, she said: “I can’t divulge that information to you. The PRO will get across to you.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The vice chancellor’s remarks are the first official acknowledgement by the institution since the publication of the investigation.

University’s earlier position

Before the publication of the report, the university had maintained that it had no information contradicting Mr Kila’s claim to the title of professor.

PREMIUM TIMES had contacted Thomas Kolo, a former registrar of the institution, seeking to speak with the university’s spokesperson. Mr Kolo passed the phone to a man who identified himself as the spokesperson but declined to disclose his name.

The spokesperson said the university had no evidence suggesting that Mr Kila was not a professor.

“We don’t debate issues. You can go up with whatever you are going up with. If there’s a need to respond, we will respond when we see the article,” he said.

The university’s pending response is expected to clarify whether it conducted any independent verification of Mr Kila’s academic rank before associating him with the title.

The issue has drawn public attention because universities are regarded as custodians of academic integrity, where claims relating to scholarly qualifications are expected to undergo rigorous checks.

World.title: One dead, another injured as tanker inferno burns shops, vehicles in Cross River
World.content:
One person has been confirmed dead while another sustained serious injuries after a petroleum tanker overturned and caught fire opposite the Odukpani Local Government Secretariat in Cross River State.

The inferno, which occurred on Sunday, also affected several shops, buildings and vehicles around the scene.

The police spokesperson, Sunday Eitokpah, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday.

According to the statement, the tanker was conveying petroleum products when it was involved in a road crash and overturned, triggering the fire.

“The driver of the tanker, who was reportedly caught in the fire, has been rescued and taken to a hospital for medical attention,” Mr Eitokpah said in the initial update.

He said police officers from the Odukpani Division were deployed to the scene to maintain safety, secure the area, and prevent further harm to members of the public.

The fire service was also alerted to deploy personnel to contain and extinguish the fire.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The police initially said no death had been confirmed, although several shops and vehicles had reportedly been affected.

However, in a subsequent update, Mr Eitokpah confirmed that one person died while another sustained serious injury and was receiving medical treatment.

The identities of the victims were not immediately disclosed.

The police urged residents, motorists and other members of the public to stay away from the immediate area to allow emergency responders unhindered access to the scene.

One in many cases

The incident adds to a series of recent fire emergencies recorded in the state.

In September, the state fire service said 17 fire incidents were recorded across the state between January and September 2026, resulting in an estimated N2.5 billion in property losses and six injuries. The incidents included a tanker spill, according to the fire service.

The state also recently witnessed a major fire at the SPAR shopping mall in Calabar on 22 August, which affected several businesses and reportedly destroyed property worth billions of naira. The federal government subsequently approved N515 million in relief for affected business owners, Channels TV reported.

Authorities have continued to urge residents to exercise caution and allow emergency agencies unhindered access during fire emergencies.

World.title: Temi Nkem wins Big Brother Naija Season 11
World.content:
Temi Nkem has emerged as the winner of the Big Brother Naija Season 11 “Show Ya Sef” season, sealing her place in the show’s history as its fifth female winner.

After 10 weeks of competition, Temi Nkem polled 25.87 per cent of the total votes from viewers in Nigeria and across Africa. The first and second runners-up, Aikou and Sheba, secured 23.68 per cent and 9.80 per cent respectively.

As the winner of BBNaija Season 11, she takes home ₦90 million in cash and a brand-new SUV, with ₦10 million from the original ₦100 million cash prize allocated to the Most Influential Player of the Week (MIPOW) prize fund.

Eventful season

The finale brought an end to a season in which 24 housemates competed through weekly tasks, Head of House games, nominations, and several twists, including some It Play and changing House veto powers each week.

The season also recorded two disqualifications and a voluntary exit, marking the first time in the show’s history that all three occurred in a single season.

Commenting on the conclusion of the season, Atinuke Babatunde, Executive Head of Content and Channels, West Africa, MultiChoice Nigeria, said:

“Season 11 has been another exciting chapter for Big Brother Naija. We saw 24 housemates bring their personalities, perspectives and individual approaches to the game, and we are pleased to have shared their journey with our viewers. We thank everyone who watched, voted and joined the conversation throughout the season, as well as our sponsors and partners for their continued support.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Big Brother Naija remains one of the continent’s most-watched reality television franchises, providing a platform that has introduced personalities who have gone on to build careers across entertainment, media, fashion, music, film, and beyond.

World.title: NPFL: Rangers stay top as Rivers United, Enyimba claim crucial wins
World.content:
Rangers International strengthened their grip on the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) summit with a 3-1 victory over Abia Warriors on Sunday, while Rivers United kept up the pressure with a 2-0 win over Ikorodu City.

The results headlined an eventful Matchday 7, which also saw Enyimba record consecutive victories, Bendel Insurance hand Barau FC their first defeat of the campaign and Kwara United come from behind to beat Ranchers Bees.

Rangers, who reclaimed top spot with a midweek victory over Warri Wolves, continued their response to an earlier defeat by Ikorodu City with a commanding display in the South-East derby at the Awka Township Stadium.

Godwin Obaje opened the scoring in the 37th minute before Chidiebere Nwobodo doubled the advantage four minutes into the second half.

Abia Warriors reduced the deficit through an Emeka Obioma penalty in the 53rd minute, but Akorode Daniel struck in stoppage time to seal the victory for the defending champions.

The win consolidates Rangers’ position at the top as they continue to play away from their traditional Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium home in Enugu, which is undergoing renovation.

Rivers United maintain pressure

Rivers United remained within striking distance of the leaders after defeating Ikorodu City 2-0 to preserve their unbeaten start.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Samson Olasupo put the Port Harcourt side ahead in the 19th minute, while Chinemerem Ugwueze added a second in first-half stoppage time.

The victory was a timely response to their 1-1 draw against Katsina United and kept Rivers firmly in the title conversation.

Enyimba build momentum

Enyimba followed their 4-2 victory over Shooting Stars with a 2-0 win against Plateau United in Aba, recording back-to-back league victories after a difficult start to the campaign.

Ifeanyi Ihemekwele gave the nine-time champions the lead in the 29th minute before Richard Ezinna sealed the result in the 68th.

The consecutive wins offer Enyimba a platform to rebuild their campaign after early struggles with goals and consistency.

Barau suffer first defeat

Barau FC’s unbeaten run ended with a 4-1 defeat at Bendel Insurance, who responded emphatically to their previous loss to Abia Warriors.

Kayode Oke scored twice, in the 33rd and 78th minutes, before Suraju Lawal and Jonathan James added late goals.

Aliyu Sugau converted a penalty for Barau in the 82nd minute, but the newcomers could not prevent their first league defeat after six matches without a loss.

Kwara, Doma claim victories

Kwara United came from behind to beat Ranchers Bees 2-1 in Ilorin.

Jamilu Yusuf gave the visitors an early lead in the seventh minute, but Toheeb Gidado equalised five minutes after the restart before Stephen Gideon completed the turnaround in the 77th minute.

Doma United also secured a narrow victory, beating Warri Wolves 1-0 at the Pantami Stadium through Joshua Abah’s 81st-minute goal.

Meanwhile, Inter Lagos and Katsina United shared the points in a 1-1 draw at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena. Nura Abdulbari put the visitors ahead in the 34th minute before Kevwe Iyede equalised eight minutes later.

Standings

Rangers International remain top of the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) table after seven matches, with 16 points and a goal difference of +5.

Rivers are second with 15 points and the league’s best goal difference of +11, while Doma United occupy third place with 13 points.

At the other end, Shooting Stars, who have a game in hand, are 17th on seven points, followed by Warri Wolves on the same tally.

Inter Lagos and Kun Khalifat occupy the two other relegation places, with five points each after seven matches.

World.title: Super Eagles lose key players as Russia friendly approaches
World.content:
The Super Eagles will be without several key players for Tuesday’s international friendly against Russia after injuries, club restrictions and travel documentation issues depleted the squad ahead of the encounter.

The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) said on Sunday that the setbacks had significantly weakened the team, with only 18 players available in Russia for the match.

Captain Wilfred Ndidi is among those ruled out after sustaining a minor injury during Nigeria’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying match against Guinea-Bissau last week.

Midfielder Raphael Onyedika was also unable to travel after his German club, Eintracht Frankfurt, reportedly stopped him from joining the squad.

Defender Bright Osayi-Samuel and UAE-based midfielder Ridwan Abdulrasaq Popoola were similarly prevented from travelling by their clubs, while Switzerland-based defender Victory Akpe was ruled out through injury.

The NFF also disclosed that Moses Usor, who scored on his Super Eagles debut against Madagascar in Uyo on 25 September, could not join the team despite a late request from head coach Éric Chelle.

Usor’s Austrian club, LASK, reportedly declined to release him for the trip to Russia.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Another absentee is Suleiman Mubarak, who was invited from Czech club Slavia Prague but could not travel because he had not secured his residence permit.

The withdrawals have left Chelle with limited options as Nigeria prepare to face Russia, nicknamed the Boys, in their second meeting in 16 months.

The teams played out a 1-1 draw at Moscow’s Luzhniki Stadium in June 2025, with Tolu Arokodare scoring Nigeria’s equaliser after Semi Ajayi’s own goal had given the hosts the lead.

Ajasa expected to join camp

The NFF said late invitee Ibraheem Ajasa of Russian club FC Rostov was expected to join the team’s camp in Nizhny Novgorod on Sunday evening.

The 18 players currently available comprise three goalkeepers, five defenders, four midfielders and six forwards.

Nigeria’s 18-man squad in Russia

Goalkeepers: Michael Atata (Ikorodu City); Samuel James (SJK FC, Finland); Stanley Nwabali (Chippa United, South Africa).

Defenders: Kenneth Igboke (Enugu Rangers); Isaac James (Alverca FC, Portugal); Benjamin Fredricks (Brentford FC, England); Emmanuel Fernandez (Glasgow Rangers, Scotland); Abdullahi Bewene (FC Banik Ostrava, Czechia).

Midfielders: Chibuzo Nwoke (Fulham FC, England); Stephen Michael (Vendsyssel FF, Denmark); Igor Wilfred (Kristiansund FC, Norway); Aderemi Adeoye (Ikorodu City).

Forwards: Kelechi Iheanacho (Bursaspor FC, Turkey); Moses Simon (Paris FC, France); Akor Adams (Venezia FC, Italy); Peter Edokpolor (SL Benfica, Portugal); Abubakar Umar (FC Famalicao, Portugal); Abdullahi Umar (Hradec Kralove, Czechia).

World.title: Oscars 2027: Nigeria submits Dear Ajayi for international feature category
World.content:
The Nigerian Official Selection Committee (NOSC) has chosen Damilola Orimogunje’s Dear Ajayi as Nigeria’s official submission for the Best International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards.

The committee announced the decision after reviewing films submitted during its month-long call for entries, which ran from 1 to 31 August.

Its selection places Dear Ajayi in contention for consideration by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences ahead of the 99th Oscars, scheduled for 14 March 2027 in Los Angeles.

The selection does not, however, constitute an Oscar nomination. The Academy will assess the film’s eligibility alongside submissions from other countries before voting determines the 15-film shortlist and, subsequently, the five nominees.

NOSC Chairperson Stephanie Linus congratulated the filmmakers and expressed the committee’s support as the production entered the next stage.

“We look forward to presenting the film for the Academy’s consideration and wish the team every success in the next stage of the process,” she said.

Nigeria returns to Oscars race

The selection marks Nigeria’s return to the Oscars process after the country failed to submit a film for the 98th Academy Awards.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In 2025, the NOSC review committee said none of the entries it considered demonstrated the required level of “creative and technical intentionality.”

The committee subsequently opened submissions for the 99th Academy Awards on 1 August, giving Nigerian filmmakers, producers, and rights holders until 31 August to enter eligible productions through its portal.

NOSC is recognised by the Academy as the body responsible for choosing Nigeria’s official entry in the International Feature Film category. The committee has overseen the country’s participation in the category since 2019.

Each year, a country or region can submit only one film through its Academy-approved selection committee. (thenosc.org)

Dear Ajayi

Written and directed by Mr Orimogunje, Dear Ajayi is a Nigeria-Germany co-production set in southwestern Nigeria in the 1990s.

The family drama follows Ade and Titi Ajayi, two estranged sisters forced to live together and care for their paralysed mother.

Ade, a devout Christian and the family’s breadwinner, struggles to understand Titi, an aspiring singer whose independent spirit challenges the expectations placed on her.

Their reunion brings old resentments to the surface, compelling both women to confront the grief, family history and conflicting ambitions that drove them apart.

The film combines Yoruba, English, and Igbo dialogue and explores family responsibility, faith, ambition, sacrifice, forgiveness, and reconciliation.

Its cast includes Bimbo Akintola as Ade, Tosin Adeyemi as Titi, and Lanre Hassan as their mother. William Benson, Antar Laniyan, Uzoamaka Power, Michelle Dede, and Chioma “Chigul” Omeruah also feature in the production.

The film featured in the competition section of the 2026 Giornate degli Autori, an independent programme held alongside the Venice International Film Festival. It is also scheduled to screen at Film Africa in London on 30 October.

Eligibility requirements

Under the Academy’s rules, an international feature must run for more than 40 minutes, be produced outside the United States and contain more than 50 per cent non-English dialogue.

Nigerian Pidgin English qualifies as a non-English language under the rules.

Entries must also carry accurate, legible English subtitles and complete a commercial cinema run of at least seven consecutive days at one venue before being released on television, streaming services, or the internet.

A prior television, online or streaming release can make a film ineligible under the theatrical-release pathway.

New festival pathway

For the 99th Academy Awards, the Academy introduced an additional qualification route for international feature films.

Under the new rule, a film not submitted through its country’s selection committee or that does not meet the normal theatrical-release requirement may still qualify independently by winning a designated award at an approved international film festival.

The qualifying festivals include Berlin, Cannes, Venice, Sundance, Toronto and Busan.

Nigeria’s Oscar history

Nigeria has not received a nomination in the Best International Feature Film category.

Its first entry, Genevieve Nnaji’s Lionheart, was disqualified from the 2020 Oscars because the Academy determined that most of its dialogue was in English.

Desmond Ovbiagele’s The Milkmaid was accepted as Nigeria’s entry for the 93rd Academy Awards but did not progress to the 15-film shortlist. Mai Mataiba also lost out in the 2025 Oscar race.

World.title: Osun govt seeks reversal of court order restricting state’s bank accounts
World.content:
The Osun State Government has asked the Federal High Court in Lagos to vacate an order restricting its bank accounts over a $13.9 million arbitration award in favour of Gamji Nigeria Company Limited, a contractor involved in water infrastructure projects in Ilesa West Local Government Area.

According to a statement signed by the state’s Commissioner of Information and Public Enlightenment, Oluomo Kolapo Alimi, and shared with PREMIUM TIMES, the government filed the application on 2 October, arguing that Gamji allegedly failed to disclose material facts when it sought the account restriction.

The state said one of the undisclosed facts was that it had already approached the Lagos State High Court to challenge the arbitration award before Gamji sought the Federal High Court order.

Mr Alimi said the state’s legal team filed the suit to set aside the arbitral award at the Lagos State High Court on 1 September, while an application was also filed to suspend enforcement of the award pending the determination of the case.

“The Counsel to the State Government had filed the suit to set aside the Arbitral Award at the Lagos State High Court since the 1st day of September, 2026 – prior to the time when Gamji Nig. Co. Ltd. surreptitiously approached the Federal High Court to deceitfully procure an ex-parte order,” Mr Alimi stated.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the Federal High Court had ordered commercial banks to place a “Post No Debit” restriction on accounts operated by the state government to preserve $13.9 million and N157.5 million awarded to Gamji.

The interim order, issued by Judge Daniel Osiagor, followed an application by Gamji Nigeria Company Limited, seeking to preserve the funds pending the determination of its motion on notice. The court adjourned the case until 22 October.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Alimi said the applications challenging the award were served on Gamji and its lawyers before the company approached the Federal High Court.

He, however, stated that the company failed to disclose the pending challenge when it sought the interim restriction on the state’s accounts.

“The state government submitted that just as the court order was a product of deceit and substantial non-disclosure of material facts to the Court, the arbitration award it sought to enforce was also fraught with several irregularities,” Mr Alimi said.

Dispute over arbitration award

The dispute arose from two water infrastructure contracts awarded to Gamji Nigeria Company Limited by the Osun State Government in 2017 during the administration of former Governor Adegboyega Oyetola.

The projects involved the construction of transmission mains and booster pump stations, as well as water reservoirs in Ilesa West Local Government Area.

Gamji Nigeria Company Limited, in its suit marked FHC/L/CS/1233/2026, told the Federal High Court that the projects were funded through an Islamic Development Bank loan facility facilitated by the Federal Ministry of Finance.

The company said the original contracts were initially valued at $15.98 million and $9.70 million, respectively, before subsequent variations increased their values.

It said about 93 per cent of the work had been completed by October 2023 and that the state government issued a Substantial Completion Certificate in November 2024.

However, disagreements later arose over claims involving extensions of time, price adjustments and increased costs of materials and labour, eventually leading to arbitration.

Gamji Nigeria Company Limited said an arbitral panel issued a final award on 24 July 2026, directing the Osun government to pay $13.9 million and N157.5 million in reimbursable arbitration fees, with 20 per cent annual interest on any outstanding balance after the compliance deadline.

Gamji subsequently approached the Federal High Court after, according to its case, the 24 August deadline for compliance expired without payment.

The Osun government, however, disputes the validity of the award and the manner in which the arbitration was conducted.

Mr Alimi said the state government was denied what it described as “fair hearing and full participation” in the arbitration process.

He said the proceedings and the eventual award were characterised by “several irregularities”, which the state has now challenged before the Lagos State High Court.

The commissioner also disputed the date and existence of an award referenced in the Federal High Court proceedings, saying there was no arbitral award against the state in July 2024 as claimed by Gamji.

“The only Arbitral Award against the State Government was in July, 2026 and the said Award is presently being challenged before the Lagos State High Court by the State Government’s legal team,” Mr Alimi said.

World.title: Tinubu visits Oba of Lagos, receives prayers, counsels
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Sunday paid a courtesy visit to the Oba of Lagos, Oba Rilwan Akiolu, at Iga Idunganran Palace, Lagos Island.

The visit provided an opportunity for the President to receive royal prayers and counsel from the traditional ruler for his administration.

Tinubu was received at the palace by members of the royal household and enthusiastic residents who gathered to welcome him.

Supporters, All Progressives Congress (APC) members and well-wishers lined the streets around Marina and Isale Eko as the President’s motorcade approached.

The gathering created a festive atmosphere, with residents cheering the President and expressing enthusiasm over his presence on Lagos Island.

The royal father offered prayers for Tinubu, his administration and the nation, seeking divine guidance and continued peace and prosperity.

Oba Akiolu also offered counsel to the President on matters concerning the country and the wellbeing of Nigerians.

The meeting underscored the traditional institution’s role in maintaining dialogue with the Federal Government and supporting national development.

Tinubu was accompanied by Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, and President’s Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila.

Also accompanying the President were APC stalwarts, political associates and other dignitaries who joined him during the visit.

The President’s visit formed part of his engagements with prominent Nigerians, traditional rulers and other stakeholders since his return to Lagos.

Tinubu returned to Lagos from his working vacation and has continued meetings with important personalities and stakeholders across different sectors.

The engagements have provided opportunities for the President to interact with influential figures and exchange views on national and state-level developments.

His meeting with Oba Akiolu further strengthened the longstanding relationship between the presidency and traditional institutions in Lagos.

The Oba of Lagos, as a prominent traditional authority, remains an influential voice on issues affecting Lagos State and the country.

The President’s presence also drew significant public attention, with residents gathering along major routes to catch a glimpse of his motorcade.

The visit ended with Tinubu departing the palace after the traditional ruler’s prayers and goodwill for the President and the country.

World.title: Portugal edge Norway to become first team through to Nations League quarter-finals
World.content:
Portugal’s forward #09 Goncalo Ramos celebrates with Portugal’s forward #11 Joao Felix and Portugal’s defender #03 Ruben Dias (L) scoring his team’s second goal during the UEFA Nations League Group 4 football match between Portugal and Norway at Dragao stadium in Porto on October 3, 2026 (Photo by Miguel RIOPA / AFP)

Portugal defeated Norway 2-1 without sulking superstar striker Cristiano Ronaldo on Sunday to qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Goncalo Ramos secured a comeback victory for Jorge Jesus’s Portugal in the Group A4 clash after Joao Cancelo’s rocket levelled Kristoffer Ajer’s stunning opener for Norway.

Portugal played out the final minutes with 10 men after Francisco Conceicao was dismissed for two yellow cards in the space of a few seconds for dissent after he appealed for a penalty unsuccessfully.

Former Real Madrid and Manchester United striker Ronaldo walked out on the squad on Wednesday ahead of the previous game against Denmark, after Portugal’s all-time top goalscorer learned he would not start.

Portugal are now guaranteed to finish in the top two spots in the group with two matches to spare, thus becoming the first team to reach the last eight in March 2027.

“Cristiano is our captain, the best player Portugal has ever had,” Cancelo told RTP.

“Things will certainly end in the best way (with Ronaldo) but the important thing is the four victories.”

Norway took the lead in Porto against the run of play with a stunning effort from Brentford defender Ajer after 36 minutes.

The Norwegian met a bouncing ball on the edge of the box perfectly to bend it into the top corner.

However two minutes later Barcelona defender Cancelo scored a similarly superb goal, rifling home from around 20 yards.

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland fired across the face of goal after an hour and was replaced by Jorgen Strand Larsen a few minutes later.

Nations League holders and two-time record champions Portugal nosed in front when AC Milan striker Ramos, starting in place of Ronaldo, tucked home from close range.

Ramos was teed up by Joao Felix, who reached Vitinha’s lofted pass and put it on a plate for the forward.

Ramos scored for a third consecutive game, and helped Portugal seal back-to-back wins since 41-year-old forward Ronaldo left the squad.

Conceicao’s foolish dismissal left Jesus’s team in a tough spot for the final few minutes. The Juventus winger was about to be replaced by Pedro Neto but his complaints led to a red card before the substitution could happen.

Portugal held on to triumph for the fourth time in four games in the group, completing a successful first international window for 72-year-old coach Jesus, despite the Ronaldo controversy.

“Any player who comes to the national team is welcome, obviously. If Cris returns, we’ll be here to receive him with open arms,” said Portugal defender Nuno Mendes.

World.title: Brazil braces for results of election battle between Lula and Bolsonaro
World.content:
A couple walks down the street wearing Brazilian national team jerseys during the presidential election in Porto Alegre, Brazil, on October 4, 2026. Brazilians head to the polls in a highly polarized presidential election between incumbent leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva -seeking a fourth presidential mandate- and right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who emerged as the leading figure of the conservative movement following the conviction and imprisonment of his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. (Photo by SILVIO AVILA / AFP)

Brazilians waited anxiously Sunday for the results of a tight election race between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro that will determine if the Latin American powerhouse joins a regional swing to the right championed by US President Donald Trump.

From the Amazon rainforest to the agricultural heartlands in the south and sprawling urban favelas, Brazilians queued to cast their vote, many of them fed-up with familiar choices.

Lula, almost 81, is seeking a fourth term in an election which he has branded a battle between democracy and “barbarism,” warning voters that Brazil’s sovereignty is at stake in the face of US pressure.
